note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Upper respiratory infection.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Andrew Campbell is a 59-year-old male with a past medical history, significant for depression, type 2 diabetes, and hypertension who presents today with an upper respiratory infection. He reports that he started feeling tired and short of breath approximately 1 week ago. He believes he caught his first cold and it just got worse. He denies fever, but notes that he felt warm. He also reports joint pain in his elbows and knees.

The patient reports that he has been doing well with his depression. His wife has been encouraging him to take barre classes to help him relax. He notes that he has been monitoring his blood sugar levels while at work, but not on weekends. He states that his diet has been good for the most part, except for house parties and other social events.

The patient reports that he has been monitoring his blood pressure at home, but not on weekends. He states that it has been under control and he is taking lisinopril as prescribed.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Respiratory: Endorses shortness of breath on exertion.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain.
• Neurological: Endorses joint pain in elbows and knees.
• Musculoskeletal: Endorses joint pain in elbows and knees.
• Gastrointestinal: Denies nausea or vomiting or diarrhea.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with ronchi present.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Chest x-ray obtained today, not yet reviewed.
Hemoglobin A1c obtained today, shows elevated at 8.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Upper respiratory infection.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today with an upper respiratory infection. His symptoms have improved over the past week without any fever or coughing up anything yet. We will send a COVID-19 test to rule out COVID-19 as the cause of his symptoms.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed the nature of his symptoms with him today and advised him to take Robitussin for cough relief and ibuprofen or Tylenol for any fever.
- Medical Treatment: We will send a COVID-19 test to rule out COVID-19 as the cause of his symptoms.
2. Depression.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient reports that he is doing well with depression at this time but would like to start medication again if needed in the future.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed the nature of his symptoms with him today and advised him to continue barre classes as they seem to be helping him relax.
- Medical Treatment: Refer him to psychotherapy if needed in the future.
3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Medical Reasoning: His hemoglobin A1c is elevated at 8 which is above target range of <7%. We will increase metformin dose from 1000 mg twice daily to 1000 mg twice daily as prescribed by me today in hopes of lowering hemoglobin A1c back down into target range by 4 months from today when we will obtain another hemoglobin A1c level.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed the nature of his symptoms with him today and advised him to continue monitoring blood sugar levels while at work but not on weekends as previously discussed in office today.
- Medical Treatment: Increase metformin dose from 1000 mg twice daily to 1000 mg twice daily as prescribed by me today in hopes of lowering hemoglobin A1c back down into target range by 4 months from today when we will obtain another hemoglobin A1c level.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Andrea Roberts is a 52-year-old female with a past medical history significant for rheumatoid arthritis, atrial fibrillation, and reflux who presents today for her annual exam. She has been walking like I told her to and exercising and doing yoga, and that has actually helped with her arthritis a lot, just the constant movement. She has not had any joint pain recently.

She is still taking methotrexate once a week without any issues. She denies any issues with the medication.

She has been having palpitations. The last one she had was about a week ago. She has noticed that when she starts to get stressed, they start to flare up again. She has been trying meditation, trying running with her dog to try and relieve the stress but it has not really been working.

She had called me last month and we did an event monitor for her, which we will take a look at in a few minutes.

Her reflux symptoms have improved. She cut out soda and that seemed to help, and the medication has been helping too. She has not had a flare up in over 5 months.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Cardiovascular: Endorses palpitations.
• Respiratory: Endorses nasal congestion due to allergies.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm at this time. Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard over the heart. No murmurs or gallops heard at auscultation of the lungs bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Event monitor results show that she is in and out of atrial fibrillation with conversion pauses. Autoimmune panel shows normal results.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Rheumatoid Arthritis.
- Medical Reasoning: Her current methotrexate prescription appears to be well tolerated without any issues.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications that may help alleviate symptoms such as walking, exercising, yoga.
- Medical Treatment: Continue methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly as prescribed.
- Additional Testing or Procedures: If needed, refer back to rheumatologist for further evaluation.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.
2. Atrial Fibrillation.
- Medical Reasoning: Due to her young age, we want to keep her in normal sinus rhythm as much as possible given that she is going in and out of atrial fibrillation at times.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications that may help alleviate symptoms such as stress reduction techniques such as meditation or running with her dog.
- Medical Treatment: Refer for cardiac ablation procedure at cardiology clinic for mapping out where the rhythm is coming from and burning it so it does not come back.
- Additional Testing or Procedures: Event monitor was already completed by the patient last month which will be reviewed today in clinic today.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.
3. Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD).
- Medical Reasoning: Her current protonix prescription appears to be effective in controlling symptoms without any issues reported by the patient since starting dietary modifications such as avoiding coffee and spicy foods.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Hyperglycemia.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Albert Powell is a 62-year-old male with a past medical history significant for depression, type 2 diabetes, and kidney transplant. He presents to the emergency room for follow-up. The patient was seen in the emergency room over the weekend due to elevated blood sugar. He was not monitoring his diet and was consuming fast food on a regular basis. He notes that he has been doing well since he returned home from the hospital visit.

The patient reports that he has been experiencing lightheadedness when he gets up from sitting or standing. He denies chest pain or shortness of breath.

The patient reports that his depression has been stable over the past year and a half. He notes that he has been doing well with his current strategies with meditation and would like to continue this for a couple more months before re-evaluating.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies lightheadedness, dizziness.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or shortness of breath.
• Psychiatric: Reports depression.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• General Examination: The patient appears well-nourished in appearance today. His vital signs are within normal limits. Pulse ox on room air. Blood pressure, and heart rate.
• Neurological Examination: No carotid bruits are appreciated. Mild 2/6 systolic ejection murmur is heard at the left sternal border. No neurological deficits are appreciated.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Hemoglobin A1c: 8%
Fasting Glucose: 162
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Hyperglycemia.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's elevated blood sugar levels are likely due to poor dietary habits and lack of monitoring of his blood glucose levels.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed dietary modifications with the patient today, including eating more frequent meals throughout the day and avoiding fast food.
- Medical Treatment: We increased his Lantus insulin dose to 20 units at night, which should help improve his blood glucose control. We also ordered another hemoglobin A1c in a couple months to monitor his progress.
2. Depression.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's current symptoms of depression are likely due to stress from recent hospitalization of his mother and lack of sleep due to busy schedule.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed relaxation techniques with the patient today, including meditation, which he has already started using successfully.
- Medical Treatment: We will hold off on medication or therapy at this time, but we will follow up in a couple months if needed.
3. Kidney Transplant Status.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's kidney function appears stable at this time based on laboratory results from last visit with Dr Reyes.

Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jerry Nguyen is a 54-year-old male with a past medical history, significant for osteoporosis and multiple sclerosis who presents for an annual exam. He has been traveling all over the country. It's been kind of a stressful summer. Kinda adjusting to everything in the fall and so far it's been good, but lack of sleep, it's been really getting to me.

The patient reports that he has tried everything from melatonin to meditation to stretching out every morning when he gets up. Nothing really seems to help though.

In terms of his osteoporosis, he is currently taking Fosamax 1 tab per week. He denies any issues with his joints or any issues like broken bones recently.

The patient last saw the neurologist 6 months ago and is taking the medication as prescribed. He denies any additional weakness, including his right leg which was previously noted to have some issues with his knee surgery but that seems to have improved.

He endorses insomnia and denies any other issues such as chest pain or shortness of breath.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain, fever, chills, or malaise.
• Neurological: Endorses insomnia.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies joint pain or swelling.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally to auscultation. No wheezes, rales, or rhonchi heard.
• Cardiovascular: Heart rate and regular in rhythm. No murmurs heard.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee obtained today shows some changes from arthritis but otherwise appears good.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Osteoporosis.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient is currently taking Fosamax 1 tab per week and has not reported any issues with his joints or broken bones recently.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of continuing on Fosamax 1 tab per week as prescribed.
- Medical Treatment: Continue on Fosamax 1 tab per week. Order a refill of fosamax 1 tab per week, 11 refills.
Multiple Sclerosis.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient last saw the neurologist 6 months ago and is taking the medication as prescribed without any additional weakness reported by him at this time.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of continuing on medications as prescribed by his neurologist.
- Medical Treatment: Continue on medications as prescribed by his neurologist.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Lawrence Walker is a 62-year-old male with a past medical history significant for type 1 diabetes, congestive heart failure, depression, and reflux. He presents with complaints of shortness of breath. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 10 days ago. He notes that he has noticed swelling in his legs. He denies any chest pain, fever, chills, or cough. He does experience some discomfort when lying flat in bed and wakes up stiff. He also notes that he wakes up acutely short of breath at night once per week.

Mr. Walker reports that he has been eating salty foods and attending house parties which he believes contribute to his current symptoms.

Regarding his diabetes, he reports that he has been monitoring his blood sugar levels regularly but notes that on weekends he forgets to monitor them. He denies any recent spike in blood sugar levels.

He reports that he has tried natural solutions for his depression but is not ready to try any medications yet.

Regarding his reflux, Mr. Walker reports that he has been making lifestyle modifications such as cutting back on red bull and caffeine and limiting alcohol intake during the holiday season.

PAST HISTORY

Type 1 diabetes.
Congestive heart failure.
Depression.
Reflux.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No jugular venous distension or carotid bruits present.
Cardiovascular: Slight grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur at the left sternal border.
Respiratory: Crackles bilaterally at the bases.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Chest X-ray: No evidence of airspace disease.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Acute heart failure exacerbation.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents with shortness of breath which began approximately 10 days ago. His physical exam reveals bilateral crackles at the bases and 1+ pitting edema in the lower extremities on examination today. His chest x-ray was reviewed today and there is no evidence of airspace disease present but this does not rule out fluid retention due to dietary indiscretion.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed the nature of his condition with him today and explained the importance of weight monitoring daily as well as calling me if his weight is not going down or if it is going up or if he gets more short of breath at rest.
- Medical Treatment: We will start him on Lasix 40 mg/day today to help reduce fluid retention. If his weight is not going down or if it is going up I want him to call me immediately or go into the emergency room for further evaluation and treatment as needed.
2. Type 1 diabetes.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents with type 1 diabetes who reports that he has been monitoring his blood sugar levels regularly but notes that on weekends he forgets to monitor them. His last hemoglobin A1c was not available for review today but we will order one in approximately a month from now to see if any adjustments are needed in his current regimen.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised him to follow up with his endocrinologist today as well as schedule a recent eye exam due to potential diabetic retinopathy risk associated with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus type 1.
- Medical Treatment: We will order a hemoglobin A1c for approximately a month from now to see if we need to make any adjustments in his current regimen.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right index finger pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Michelle James is a 42-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right index finger pain. The onset of her symptoms began 5 days ago, when she sustained an injury while skiing. She was skiing down a double black diamond trail and lost control, flipping down a few ways. She believes she jammed her right index finger on something during this incident. The patient reports that she has not taken any medication for her symptoms, despite trying ibuprofen which did not provide relief. She has also not applied ice or used a splint on her finger.

The patient rates her pain as a 7 out of 10. She denies any other injuries sustained during the skiing incident.

The patient reports that she has chronic constipation and notes that MiraLAX helps with this symptom.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that she had an appendectomy at age 7.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she takes MiraLAX for chronic constipation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right index finger pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MSK: Examination of the right hand reveals normal distal interphalangeal joint mobility with pain to palpation over the joint. No evidence of fractures or dislocations.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-rays of the right index finger were obtained today and reviewed in office today. These reveal no evidence of fractures or dislocations.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Right index finger sprain.
- Medical Reasoning: The x-ray examination revealed no evidence of fractures or dislocations, but there is evidence of joint effusion and swelling consistent with a sprain of the distal interphalangeal joint (DIP) joint.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the nature of her injury and treatment options in detail today.
- Medical Treatment: We placed a splint on her right hand today. I have also prescribed Mobic 15 mg once daily for 14 days to help reduce inflammation and pain associated with her injury. I want to see her again in 2 weeks to check on healing progress at which point we can discuss hand therapy if necessary.
- Additional Testing: X-rays were obtained today.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Cheryl Ramirez is a 34-year-old female with a past medical history significant for hypertension. She presents today with back pain.

The onset of her back pain began 6 days ago when she was walking. She describes the onset as a sudden clenching sensation in her back. She denies any trauma or lifting prior to the onset of her pain. She has been lifting more than usual, approximately 3 times per week, and suspects that this may have contributed to her back pain. The patient reports that she has been taking ibuprofen and applying heat to the area, but the pain persists.

The patient denies any lower extremity numbness, tingling, or weakness in her legs or feet. She also denies any fever, chills, congestion, cough, chest pain, or shortness of breath.

The patient reports that she has been walking for 30 minutes to an hour per day and notes that she has been doing well with her blood pressure at home. She reports that she has been watching her diet and notes that her boyfriend has also been dieting with her.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever, chills.
• Respiratory: Endorses nasal congestion from seasonal allergies.
• Musculoskeletal: Endorses back pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Cardiovascular: Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at auscultation over the left sternal border. Stable from previous exams.
• Musculoskeletal: Pain to palpation on the right lateral aspect of the lumbar spine. Pain with flexion and extension as well. Negative straight leg raise.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Back x-ray obtained today in office review is unremarkable for any obvious fractures or bony abnormalities.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Lumbar strain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's history and physical exam findings are consistent with a lumbar strain. The onset of her symptoms began after increased activity level which may have caused overuse of the lumbar spine.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed treatment options with the patient today including prescription medication and referral to physical therapy for strengthening exercises of the back.
- Medical Treatment: Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily to treat pain associated with lumbar strain. Patient can ice area as needed and apply heat sometimes as well.
2. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood pressure is well controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily at home.

Left shoulder and elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. James is a 64-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of left shoulder and elbow pain. He reports that he fell 5 months ago while going up stairs, and has had constant pain in his left shoulder and elbow since then. The pain is present at all times, but is worse at times. He notes that he has been trying to keep up with his weightlifting routine, but has had to stop due to the pain. He states that he has tried icing and stopping exercise, which has provided some relief.

The onset of his symptoms began 5 months ago when he fell while going up stairs. He states that it was icy and he stepped out with his feet. He landed on his left side and believes that his left shoulder and wrist took the brunt of the fall. He notes that he has not been able to lift more than 20 pounds due to the pain.

The patient denies any numbness or tingling in his left arm or hand.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left shoulder and elbow pain.

Impingement syndrome of left shoulder.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Upper respiratory infection.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Randy Gutierrez is a 9-month-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of an upper respiratory infection. He was seen in clinic yesterday and today. The onset of his symptoms began around supper time last night. He started to get a runny nose, and he is currently clear of mucous. He also has a cough, but it is not barky. He has been pulling on his ears, and he has been going crazy rubbing at his nose too.

The patient’s rectal temperature was 100.3 degrees this morning. His appetite has been variable, with him eating 7 ounces from the bottle this morning and then another bottle where he barely ate that. He also refused cereal this morning.

The patient is irritable due to not feeling well, but he does have good energy when he is napping. His older sister has been sick with a sinus infection.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient’s older sister has been sick with a sinus infection.

MEDICATIONS

Tylenol PRN.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Respiratory: Denies barking cough.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or difficulty breathing.
• Gastrointestinal: Reports refusal of cereal this morning.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezes or rales are heard.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Randy Gutierrez is a 9-month-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of an upper respiratory infection.
• Medical Reasoning: The onset of his symptoms began around supper time last night. He started to get a runny nose, and he is currently clear of mucous. He also has a cough, but it is not barky. He has been pulling on his ears, and he has been going crazy rubbing at his nose too.
• Additional Testing/Examination: All necessary testing was completed in office today.
• Medical Treatment: We discussed treatment options for today’s visit in detail with the patient’s mother. We have prescribed Tylenol PRN as needed for fever control and Zarbee’s for nasal congestion relief at home today as well as giving her some Tylenol PRN as well since they are probably sharing the same virus at home.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options in detail with the patient’s mother today including using saline mist in Randy’s nose, baby Vick’s on his feet, humidifier use at home, cradle cap brush use along with regular Aveno shampoo twice per week, and avoiding honey due to botulism spores which can cause harm in infants under 1 year old but agave nectar can be used instead as long as it does not contain honey or any other ingredients that could cause harm in infants under 1 year old such as honey nut cheerios which contains real honey.
• Special Instructions: Continue to monitor Randy for signs of worsening symptoms such as barking cough if present.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Acne.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kayla Ward is a 15-year-old female who presents for a new visit with her mother for acne located on the face, which started about 2 years ago and is present most every day. She has been using Persa-Gel and washing regularly, which is somewhat helpful. There are no associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain.

The patient denies any flare-ups with her periods. She reports that she gets a regular period and has been getting one for approximately 2 years. Her biggest flare was when she started school sports in the fall due to all the sweating.

The patient's skin care routine includes washing her face with water and a washcloth in the morning, followed by an Elf facial cleanser called Super Clarity cleanser. She finishes with a toner and then Persa-Gel at night. She notes that this regimen has been somewhat helpful but not as much as they had hoped.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Skin: Denies itching, bleeding, or pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Multiple benign nevi on the trunk and extremities.
Scattered skin-colored papules.
Open and closed comedones.
Erythematous papules on the face, primarily on the forehead and central cheeks and chin.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Kayla Ward is a 15-year-old female who presents for a new visit with her mother for acne located on the face, which started about 2 years ago and is present most every day. She has been using Persa-Gel and washing regularly, which is somewhat helpful. There are no associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain.

Multiple benign nevi on the trunk and extremities were noted on exam today.
Scattered skin-colored papules were noted on exam today.
Open and closed comedones were noted on exam today.
Erythematous papules on the face were noted primarily on the forehead and central cheeks and chin today.
The chest and back are relatively spared from acne today.
The remainder of the examination was normal.
Mild to moderate acne was seen today mostly comodonal with small inflammatory component.
INSTRUCTIONS AND FOLLOW-UP CARE

We discussed treatment options in detail today. I have prescribed adapalene 0.1% cream to be used in a thin layer to areas where she generally gets acne 3-4 times per week initially then increase to nightly use if tolerated without any adverse effects. If this is too expensive or not covered by insurance she can try different gel over-the-counter. Clean & Clear Persa-Gel can be used in thin layer over adapalene if needed followed by non-comedogenic moisturizer. Adapalene will cause some sensitivity so sunscreen will need to be worn when outside. It may also cause some dryness or irritation.
We will see if there is any progress over the next 6 months at that time.

Skin: Denies itching, bleeding, or pain.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Kayla Ward is a 15-year-old female who presents for a new visit with her mother for acne located on the face, which started about 2 years ago and is present most every day. She has been using Persa-Gel and washing regularly, which is somewhat helpful. There are no associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain.

Multiple benign nevi on the trunk and extremities were noted on exam today.
Scattered skin-colored papules were noted on exam today.
Open and closed comedones were noted on exam today.
Erythematous papules on the face were noted primarily on the forehead and central cheeks and chin today.
The chest and back are relatively spared from acne today.
The remainder of the examination was normal.
Mild to moderate acne was seen today mostly comodonal with small inflammatory component.
INSTRUCTIONS AND FOLLOW-UP CARE

We discussed treatment options in detail today. I have prescribed adapalene 0.1% cream to be used in a thin layer to areas where she generally gets acne 3-4 times per week initially then increase to nightly use if tolerated without any adverse effects. If this is too expensive or not covered by insurance she can try different gel over-the-counter. Clean & Clear Persa-Gel can be used in thin layer over adapalene if needed followed by non-comedogenic moisturizer. Adapalene will cause some sensitivity so sunscreen will need to be worn when outside. It may also cause some dryness or irritation.
We will see if there is any progress over the next 6 months at that time.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Breast reduction.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female who presents for evaluation of breast reduction. She has been experiencing back pain and neck pain for approximately 5 years, which she believes may be related to her breasts. She has been wearing a 34E sports bra due to discomfort and difficulty finding a regular bra in her size. The patient denies any nipple pain or numbness in the hands. She reports that she has been trying to lose weight, but has only lost 10 pounds over the past few months. The patient is currently studying to be a psychologist.

The patient reports that she has had no children and does not plan on having any children in the future. She denies any rashes underneath her breasts, but notes that they are always sweaty.

The patient reports that she experiences back pain when she holds her breasts while working out or running. She has been seeing a chiropractor for several years, but denies any physical therapy for her back pain.

The patient reports that she takes propranolol for migraine prevention.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that her mother had breast cancer at age 40. The patient notes that she started getting mammograms at age 30, but is still only 25 years old.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she is currently studying to be a psychologist and drinks one glass of wine per week.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Musculoskeletal: Reports back pain and neck pain.
• Skin: Denies rashes underneath her breasts, but notes they are always sweaty.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Breast: Inspection reveals asymmetrical breasts with severe ptosis bilaterally. There is no nipple retraction or discharge bilaterally. No breast tenderness, masses, or axillary lymphadenopathy is palpable.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Breast reduction.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient is an ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty due to her extremely large breasts and the presence of severe ptosis bilaterally. Her minimum required resection based on BSA of 2.65 with Schnur scale is 1,792 grams, which should be attainable given her large breasts and measurements above there is potential for using a nipple graft.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the risks and benefits of breast reduction surgery in detail today including potential complications such as infection, seroma formation, scarring, implant rupture, capsular contracture, nipple sensation changes and changes in breast size after pregnancy or breastfeeding. We also discussed the importance of smoking cessation prior to surgery as well as avoiding heavy lifting for 6 weeks postoperatively.
• Medical Treatment: No medical treatment was recommended today.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Hematuria.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mrs. Kelly Wood is a 41-year-old female who presents for renal ultrasound due to hematuria. The patient reports that she has had bright red urine for the past 6 weeks, and she was constantly having to urinate and it hurt terribly. She denies flank pain or lower back tenderness at this time. She notes that she passed 2 small stones last week after scheduling this appointment.

The patient is a chronic urolithiasis patient.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she drinks more Mountain Dew than water.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that she is taking Alavert 10 mg tablet once daily.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss, fever, chills, or malaise.
• Genitourinary: Reports hematuria.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies flank pain or lower back tenderness.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Abdomen: No flank pain. Anti-Guernsey exam is normal.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• Urine dipstick today: Color yellow and clear, urobilinogen 0.2 EU/dL, pH 5.5 and specific gravity 1.020.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Primary diagnosis: Hematuria.
• Secondary diagnosis: Chronic urolithiasis.
• Medical Reasoning: The blood in the urine was due to the kidney stones. Fortunately, the patient passed two last week and the blood has nearly subsided. She does still have one stone in the left kidney. Since it's not obstructing or causing pain, I do not recommend any surgical intervention at this time.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the formation of kidney stones can not be attributed to a particular cause but several factors increase the risk such as dehydration, family history, certain foods, digestive tract disease and certain medical conditions. The patient should drink about half of her body weight in ounces of water a day. She should avoid drinking sugary drinks like Mountain Dew. She should also avoid food rich in sodium oxalate and animal protein such as salty processed food because they are high in sodium and reduce the amount of beef poultry fish and pork to less than 1000 mg per day.
• Additional Testing/Procedures: Repeat renal ultrasound in 1 year if symptoms persist or if there are any issues with bleeding or pain.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Status post mitral valve repair.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Melissa Sanchez is a 58-year-old female who presents for a follow-up status post mitral valve repair. She was seen in office on 9/17/2020, at which time we felt that she was doing quite well from a cardiac standpoint, and so we recommended she continue with the same medication. ECG taken on 12/26/2020 reveals atrial fibrillation with a controlled ventricular response. T-wave inversion anteriorly. Compared to the previous study, there are no significant changes.

The patient reports that she is feeling better overall since surgery. She notes that she was having a rough time before surgery but thinks she is doing well now. She denies any new symptoms at this time. She does report experiencing chest pain sometimes and her breathing gets shallow, but she has learned what she can and cannot do and if she feels like exerting herself, she slows down a bit which helps, and then when she goes back to it later, she can usually finish whatever it was that she was doing.

She estimates that these episodes last only a few minutes and then they disappear for a couple of weeks. When they happen, she just takes the day nice and slow and does not push herself. She estimates that these episodes occur often enough for her to notice.

The patient reports taking her medications regularly. She states that there are extra pills now but has a reminder app so she does well with this.

She denies any side effects from the medications at this time except for the atenolol which makes her irritable initially but does not seem to bother her as much now.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Respiratory: Denies dyspnea on exertion.
• Cardiovascular: Reports chest pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Head and Neck: No JVD detected in left neck extensor sternocleidomastoid area.
• Respiratory: Reduced breath sounds bilaterally without wheezes or rales; Auscultation of Lungs clear to auscultation; No wheezes or rales heard bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
ECG taken on 12/26/2020 reveals atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response. T-wave inversion anteriorly. Compared to the previous study, there are no significant changes.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Status post mitral valve repair.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient is doing well from a cardiac standpoint at this point in time. Her ECG shows atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response but no significant changes compared to the previous study.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications such as regular exercise which will help improve cardiac function.
• Medical Treatment: Continue Coumadin 4 mg daily; Lasix 40 mg daily; Atenolol 50 mg daily as prescribed.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Judy Gomez is a 61-year-old female who presents for ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis. She reports that her pain has been well-controlled on methotrexate, but she has been taking prednisone 1 mg daily. She notes that she was taking 2 mg prednisone for a couple of days due to increased pain in her feet, but this was only once a week. She denies any other changes in her medication regimen.

The patient reports that she has noticed an improvement in her joint pain since increasing the dose of methotrexate. However, she did experience a significant decrease in efficacy with the first dose of methotrexate due to concerns about COVID-19 vaccine efficacy. She was advised by the hotline to continue with the medication and did so without issue. The patient is currently not scheduled for blood work and will follow up in 3 months.

The patient denies any other symptoms or concerns at this time.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports joint pain.
Skin: Reports ridges in nails due to psoriasis.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Skin: Examination of the skin reveals ridges in nails consistent with psoriasis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Judy Gomez is a 61-year-old female who presents for ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis.

Medical Reasoning: The patient's current symptoms are consistent with psoriatic arthritis. Her improvement on methotrexate is noted, but she did experience a significant decrease in efficacy with the first dose due to concerns about COVID-19 vaccine efficacy. We have discussed alternative treatment options and will discontinue prednisone today and continue with methotrexate as prescribed.
Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the risks associated with prednisone use, including increased bruising, and advised her to stop by the front desk to schedule an appointment for blood work.
Additional Testing: Schedule blood work at the front desk.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Newly diagnosed heart murmur.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Diana Scott is a 100-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for a new patient evaluation. The patient reports that she was recently seen by her primary care physician and was told that she has a new worrisome heart murmur. She denies any chest pain or shortness of breath. She does report severe leg pain, which started about a month ago. She has been taking pain medication for this. The patient also reports that she gets short of breath if she walks too fast or too long, or if she tries to drink a whole glass of water without stopping. She estimates that her symptoms have improved 70-80% over the past 6 months compared to 1 year ago when she did not notice anything at all.

The patient reports that she is using a walker due to her leg pain and shortness of breath.

The patient denies lightheadedness or dizziness, but admits to taking medication for this when it does get bad.

She denies any passing out at all.

The patient denies irregular heartbeats, but admits to taking medication for this as well.

She reports swelling in her ankles.

The patient reports weight loss over the past year, but notes that her weight has been stable lately.

She denies fevers, chills, or any other symptoms.

PAST HISTORY

Family history of heart disease.
Son had myocardial infarction.
Brother had a stroke and has diabetes.
Older sister has an unknown heart problem.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Constitutional Elderly Otherwise No Acute Distress. Cardiovascular Normal S1 and S2 is preserved with a normal rate and regular rhythm. There is a 4/6 systolic murmur at the right upper sternal border with mild radiation to the carotids.

Newly diagnosed heart murmur.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Diana Scott is a 100-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for a new patient evaluation. The patient reports that she was recently seen by her primary care physician and was told that she has a new worrisome heart murmur. She denies any chest pain or shortness of breath. She does report severe leg pain, which started about a month ago. She has been taking pain medication for this. The patient also reports that she gets short of breath if she walks too fast or too long, or if she tries to drink a whole glass of water without stopping. She estimates that her symptoms have improved 70-80% over the past 6 months compared to 1 year ago when she did not notice anything at all.

The patient reports that she is using a walker due to her leg pain and shortness of breath.

The patient denies lightheadedness or dizziness, but admits to taking medication for this when it does get bad.

She denies any passing out at all.

The patient denies irregular heartbeats, but admits to taking medication for this as well.

She reports swelling in her ankles.

The patient reports weight loss over the past year, but notes that her weight has been stable lately.

She denies fevers, chills, or any other symptoms.

PAST HISTORY

Family history of heart disease.
Son had myocardial infarction.
Brother had a stroke and has diabetes.
Older sister has an unknown heart problem.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Newly diagnosed allergic asthma.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Charles Sullivan is a 45-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of new onset shortness of breath. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 2 years ago when he moved into a large plot of land in the city. He enjoys hunting and has a refrigerator full of venison at home. He notes that he has noticed that his breathing is not what it used to be, and he considers himself to be pretty healthy. He denies any previous issues with allergies.

The patient reports that he gets shortness of breath suddenly for no apparent reason. He notes that his eyes water when he gets eyebugers, which are common in his dog. He denies any rash with his symptoms and notes that he does not have nausea or vomiting, except when he goes out heavy drinking, which results in diarrhea.

The patient denies any lip or throat swelling and notes that he does not have any symptoms now when he travels.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Respiratory: Reports shortness of breath.
• Allergic: Denies any known allergies.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with mild expiratory wheezing.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Chest x-ray obtained today was normal.
Pulmonary function test obtained today was normal.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Newly diagnosed allergic asthma.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's chest x-ray and pulmonary function test were both normal, but the physical exam reveals mild expiratory wheezing bilaterally in all lung fields. This suggests asthma.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the nature of his diagnosis in detail today. I advised him to continue using his albuterol inhaler as prescribed and to take Singulair 10 mg once daily as prescribed by my office staff. I also advised him to avoid triggers such as dust mites, mold, pet dander, etc., until we can determine what his specific allergen is through allergy testing.
• Medical Treatment: Continue albuterol inhaler as prescribed. Prescribed Singulair 10 mg once daily.
• Additional Testing: Allergy testing will be performed next week.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Low back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Bryan Brooks is a 39-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of low back pain. The onset of his pain began 2 hours ago when he was raking leaves in his yard. He denies any prior history of similar episodes. He notes that he has had an episode of low back pain 3 years ago, which resolved after a day.

The patient reports that he has been doing minimal physical activity lately and that his partner has also been doing minimal yard work. He denies any history of trauma or injury to the back.

The patient describes his pain as radiating down to his right foot, with some improvement with sitting and worsening with standing and bending over. He notes that applying ice and taking Advil did not provide relief. He reports that a hot shower provides some relief.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that he had an episode of low back pain 3 years ago, which resolved after a day.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Mr. Brooks is married and reports that his partner is also experiencing low back pain when he stands up.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological Examination: Gait: Normal gait without evidence of weakness or spasticity. Motor Strength: Normal motor strength in all extremities bilaterally. Sensation: Intact light touch sensation in all extremities bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-rays of the low back were obtained today and are pending review.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Low back strain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with low back strain, likely secondary to overexertion while raking leaves in the yard.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the nature of her diagnosis, treatment options, and lifestyle modifications she can make to prevent future episodes.
- Medical Treatment: We have prescribed meloxicam for pain management and physical therapy to improve strength, flexibility, and range of motion.
- Additional Testing: We will follow up in 2 weeks if her symptoms do not improve.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Non-healing right foot ulcer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Hernandez is a 40-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer. The patient reports that he has had the ulcer for approximately 2 months and it has recently become red and is draining. He denies any trauma to his foot when he got it, but believes that he may have gotten it from walking barefoot on the beach.

The patient states that he did see his primary care physician before coming in today, and they prescribed him medication for his ulcer. However, he has not yet picked up the medication from the pharmacy.

The patient reports that his ulcer sometimes throbs, but he does not have specific pain. He notes that his biggest concern is that it started to drain and it looks a little red. He has not had this before.

The patient reports that he takes his diabetes medication, but he does not check his blood sugar levels regularly. He estimates that his last A1C was around 10.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Skin: Reports redness and drainage from the ulcer.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• General Examination: Vital signs are within normal limits. No fever present.
• Foot Examination: There is a 1 x 2 inch circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot, proximal to the 5th MTP joint. There is some redness and drainage present. There is edema around it, with fluid leaking out of it. I do not see any necrosis or odor. I do not appreciate any bony exposure.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right foot was performed prior to today's visit, which shows no evidence of osteomyelitis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Mr. Hernandez is a 40-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's current symptoms are consistent with an infected diabetic foot ulcer.
• Additional Testing: An ABI ankle brachial index will be ordered to determine blood supply in his foot.
• Medical Treatment: Debridement will be performed today to remove dead tissue from the wound site. Clindamycin will be prescribed for 7 days at 400 mg twice daily to treat infection.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed with him how wearing regular shoes can irritate this area and cause further complications if left untreated.
• Additional Testing/Interventions: We will obtain a shoe for him to wear while this is healing up at home.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left ankle pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Stephanie Morales is a 36-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of left ankle pain. The onset of her symptoms began 2 days ago when she slipped and fell on her left ankle while walking to her car. She states that she twisted her ankle on the outside of her hip. She was able to get up afterwards but it was very sore and started swelling and quite a bit of pain, making it hard to walk.

The patient has tried ibuprofen, ice, and elevation which have provided some relief. She denies any pain above her ankle, such as in her calf or lower leg or knee.

The patient reports that she has been taking metformin for type 2 diabetes and that her blood sugars have been stable. She states that she has been cutting back on sweets and sugars and exercising regularly. Her last hemoglobin A1c was 6.8, which is good. She is due for an eye exam in the next couple of weeks.

The patient reports that she has been taking Norvasc for hypertension and that her blood pressure has been stable today at 120/70 mmHg. She needs a refill on this medication.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left ankle pain.
Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
Neurological: Denies any neurological deficits.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: Supple without bruits.
Lungs: Clear bilaterally to auscultation.
Heart: Normal with grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur unchanged from previous exams.
Abdomen: Normal without hepatomegaly or splenomegaly.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the left ankle reveals tenderness over the lateral malleolus and tenderness over the fifth metatarsal bone. There is some swelling, redness, and pain with valgus stressing of the ankle.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the left ankle will be ordered.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Left ankle sprain with possible fracture.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's examination revealed tenderness over the lateral malleolus and fifth metatarsal bone with swelling, redness, and pain with valgus stressing of the ankle. These findings are consistent with an ankle sprain but also raise concern for a fracture. An x-ray will be ordered to evaluate for this possibility.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options in detail today including wearing an air splint until we receive x-ray results, crutches until then, weight-bearing avoidance until x-ray results are available, naprosyn 500 mg twice daily for pain control, elevation, ice application, and continued exercise as tolerated.
- Medical Treatment Plan: We will order an x-ray of the left ankle today. If there is no fracture present we will remove the air splint and allow partial weight-bearing as tolerated. If there is a fracture present we will refer to orthopedics at that time.
The patient will continue with metformin as prescribed by another provider due to stable blood sugars at this point in time. We discussed continuing regular checking of blood sugars as well as dietary modifications as previously discussed. The patient is due for an eye exam in 2 weeks which she already has scheduled at this time so no further action is needed regarding this appointment today.
The patient's blood pressure was stable at 120/70 mmHg today at this point in time so no further action is needed regarding this medication refills today.

note.objective_results:

Mr. William Russell is a 57-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of his pain began 1 week ago when he sustained an injury at a trampoline park. He states that he heard a pop and instant pain when he was on the trampoline. He denies any previous history of trampoline park injuries. He notes that he does not regularly work out and this is his first time engaging in such activity.

The patient reports that his right knee pain is worse on the lateral aspect of the knee. He denies any improvement with Tylenol and has only elevated his knee.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that he has hypertension and type 2 diabetes.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he does not regularly exercise and only engages in recreational activities such as going to the trampoline park.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain, dyspnea, or orthopnea.
Gastrointestinal: Denies nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain.
Genitourinary: Denies urinary frequency, urgency, or incontinence.
note.objective_exam:

CV: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee revealed no evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right knee pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient sustained an injury at a trampoline park which resulted in lateral ligament strain. This is a common injury that tends to heal on its own with conservative treatment.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the nature of his injury and treatment options in detail today.
- Medical Treatment: We have prescribed meloxicam 15 mg daily for pain and swelling. We have also referred him to physical therapy to help strengthen the muscles around the area and prevent further injury if necessary.
- Additional Testing: X-ray of the right knee was ordered today which revealed no evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.
2. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: His blood pressure is elevated at 180/80 mmHg today which may be due to inadequate medication compliance or non-adherence with lifestyle modifications such as diet and exercise.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications with him today including dietary changes, increased physical activity, weight loss if necessary, stress reduction techniques, etc., as well as medication adherence.
- Medical Treatment: We will continue him on lisinopril 20 mg daily for now but will need to re-evaluate his blood pressure soon due to elevated readings today. An echocardiogram will be ordered for further evaluation.
3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Medical Reasoning: His blood sugar levels appear to be improving but we need more information regarding long-term control of his diabetes mellitus. His A1c level will be ordered for further evaluation as well as a lipid panel.

The epidural steroid injection will be placed at the level of L4-5 where we have seen evidence of nerve root impingement on MRI studies today.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Headaches.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

The patient is a 33-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of headaches. She reports that she has been experiencing headaches since she was a teenager, initially during her menstrual periods, but now more frequently and severely. These headaches are aggravated by physical activities. The patient notes that she has noticed an increase in frequency and severity of her headaches over the past few months. She also reports that she has been trying to exercise more in order to lose weight, but she is unable to exercise for very long because her headaches return and are worse.

The patient also reports that she has been experiencing ringing in her ears for a few months now, and recently started experiencing some blurred vision. The blurred vision is intermittent and appears to be on the side of her vision.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Neurological: Reports ringing in her ears, blurred vision.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports numbness or tingling in her hands or feet.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Cardiovascular: Normal sinus rhythm with no murmurs, gallops.
• Neurological: Cranial nerves 1-12 are intact including normal cranial reflexes. Gait is normal.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Idiopathic intracranial hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are concerning for idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH). Her symptoms include worsening headaches with activity, tinnitus, and changes in vision. These symptoms are concerning for increased intracranial pressure.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the nature of IIH, its treatment options, and lifestyle modifications that can help alleviate symptoms.
- Medical Treatment: We will obtain a recent MRI of the brain to confirm the diagnosis. If this confirms IIH, we will start medical treatment with medications to decrease intracranial pressure. We will also refer the patient to a neuro-ophthalmologist for a complete eye exam.
- Additional Testing: We will obtain a lumbar puncture to evaluate intracranial pressure.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Neck pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Jack Torres is a pleasant 40-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of neck pain. The onset of his pain began approximately 1 week ago when he was involved in a motor vehicle accident. He states that he was struck from behind and his neck went forward and his head went forward quickly. He denies any other injuries at the time of the accident. The patient reports that he has been experiencing pain in the back of his neck, which is rated as a 7 out of 10 in terms of severity. He notes that the pain is not constant but worsens with movement of his neck. He has tried ibuprofen, which has provided some relief, but not to a great extent.

The patient denies any headaches or visual disturbances. He also denies any hearing problems.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left-sided neck pain.
Neurological: Denies headaches, visual disturbances, and hearing problems.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck Examination: Positive to palpation over the left side of the neck with flexion and extension. Positive to palpation over the left side of the neck with lateral bending.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of cervical spine obtained today, not yet reviewed.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

After reviewing the patient's examination and radiographic findings today, I have had a lengthy discussion with him regarding his symptoms and treatment options.

The patient's examination revealed evidence of left-sided cervical strain.
In terms of treatment options, I have recommended that we start conservatively with anti-inflammatories (Motrin 600 mg) to be taken every 6-8 hours as needed for pain control. I have also recommended that he take Flexeril (10 mg) every 12 hours as needed for muscle relaxation.
I advised him to avoid straining his neck further by being conservative with how he moves about and everything like that.
I have also ordered an MRI due to his denial of seeking medical attention after his motor vehicle accident and because we are concerned about possible concussion or whiplash injury.
I referred him to either physical rehabilitation or chiropractic care once we receive the results of his MRI for further evaluation and treatment if necessary.

The patient states that his current symptoms are more on the outside of his right shoulder and are tender to palpation. He notes that there is no restriction with his arm, but he does feel pain on the outside of it when he moves it. His symptoms are worse with movement, but not at rest. He notes that he sleeps on his right side and this may be contributing to his symptoms at night.

The patient reports that he has been taking Advil and icing as much as possible for pain relief. This has provided some relief, but the pain is still present to palpation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left shoulder pain.
Neurological: Denies numbness in the left arm or hands.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Asthma.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Betty Lewis is a 66-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of asthma. She reports that she has been experiencing symptoms of asthma for the past 6 months. She states that she has been coughing and wheezing almost every day. She notes that she wakes up 2-3 times per week and needs to use her inhaler. She also reports that she wakes up 1-2 times per week and needs to use her inhaler again. She denies any improvement in her symptoms despite using her inhaler as needed.

She notes that her symptoms seem to worsen when she gets sick, but she does not know what triggers this. She does note that when she visited her aunt's house, she had a flare-up after being around her cat, so she tries to avoid going there.

She reports that she has been to urgent care several times for her asthma symptoms and has been prescribed antibiotics on some occasions. She also notes that on one occasion, she was hospitalized due to an asthma exacerbation when she was 8 years old.

She denies any history of seasonal allergies. She does enjoy going outside and hiking, but notes that due to her coughing and wheezing, she is careful not to overdo it.

PAST HISTORY

History of asthma.
No history of seasonal allergies.
No history of smoking or tobacco use.
No history of vaping or e-cigarette use.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Respiratory: Diminished lung sounds throughout with occasional slight expiratory wheeze bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Pulmonary function test obtained today, not yet reviewed.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Moderate intermittent asthma.
• Medical Reasoning: Her symptoms are consistent with moderate intermittent asthma.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of consistent use of inhaled steroid inhaler and how this will help reduce daily symptoms and need for rescue inhaler less frequently. We also discussed the importance of using albuterol inhaler only as needed in case of an acute exacerbation.
• Medical Treatment: I have started you on fluticasone 100 mcg one puff twice per day which will be important for you to be consistent with your inhaled steroid inhaler this is going to help prevent those daily symptoms from needing for you to use your albuterol inhaler less frequently you can continue using your ventolin inhaler as needed two puffs every 4-6 hours p.r.n.
• Additional Testing: Review of pulmonary function test results which are consistent with someone who would be diagnosed with asthma.
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Chronic lumbar back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Larry Garcia is a 41-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of chronic lumbar back pain. The onset of his pain began approximately 2 years ago when he was moving furniture. He describes his pain as sharp stabbing in nature, radiating down to his right leg and even down to his right toe. He also reports difficulty getting comfortable, which is worse when he sits down. He denies any numbness or tingling in the genital or rectal area, as well as weakness. He denies any loss of control of his bladder or bowels.

The patient has tried various treatments for his back pain, including physical therapy and strong pain medications. He has also been advised on surgery but he would like to avoid this option.

The patient reports that he is trying to be as active as possible but due to his back pain, he has gained weight over the past few years. He used to enjoy playing golf but this has set him back from continuing with this activity.

PAST HISTORY

• Chronic lumbar back pain.
• Quit smoking 20 years ago.
• Denies any family history of spine conditions.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal: Examination of the musculoskeletal system reveals no erythema or ecchymosis over the skin. There is midline tenderness at L4-L5 disk space with right-sided lumbar paravertebral tenderness. Supine straight leg test is positive.
Neurological: Examination of the neurological system reveals decreased sensation to light touch at L4 dermatome on the right lateral thigh.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

MRI of the lumbar spine shows disc herniation with nerve impingement.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Mr. Larry Garcia is a 41-year-old male who presents today for the evaluation of chronic lumbar back pain.
1) Medical Reasoning: His symptoms are consistent with an L4-L5 herniated disk with radiculopathy.
2) Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options in detail today including a spinal injection with a corticosteroid under fluoroscopy which should help reduce inflammation causing his pain.
3) Medical Treatment: I have recommended that we proceed with a spinal injection with a corticosteroid under fluoroscopy today if that works for him if not we will get him scheduled for his first injection.
4) Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Incidental finding of a right upper lobe lung nodule.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

The patient is a 57-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of an incidental finding of a right upper lobe lung nodule on his CT scan of the chest. He reports that he has been experiencing a cough for approximately 3 months, which he initially noticed when he was loading horses. He denies any previous history of lung infections or pneumonia.

The patient reports that he exercises regularly, biking approximately 60 miles per week, and notes that he typically does not get sick. His cough has resolved with the onset of a cold. He denies any pain or shortness of breath.

The patient reports that he has a history of rheumatoid arthritis, which is currently well-controlled with methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly. He notes that his joints are generally well-controlled, but he does experience some hand pain.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that he was a previous smoker and stopped smoking approximately 7 years ago. His mother has a history of breast cancer, but is doing well.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Respiratory: Denies dyspnea or shortness of breath.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies pain in the extremities.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• CT scan of chest demonstrates a solitary 2 cm nodule in the lateral aspect of the right upper lobe.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Incidental finding of right upper lobe lung nodule.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for the evaluation of an incidental finding on his CT scan of the chest demonstrating a solitary 2 cm nodule in the lateral aspect of the right upper lobe. Given his smoking history, I believe it is most likely malignant in nature.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options in detail today and I have provided him with additional information regarding his options.
- Medical Treatment: I have ordered pulmonary function testing (PFT) to obtain baseline lung function. We will also schedule a PET CT to determine if this nodule is metabolically active. I have also recommended removal via video-assisted thoracoscopy due to his smoking history and because it will allow us to obtain tissue for histopathological examination if needed. This will be performed under general anesthesia and will take approximately 1 hour and post-procedure. The patient will be admitted overnight and we will remove the chest tube at bedside on post-op day 1.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Difficulty swallowing.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Tyler Green is a 56-year-old male who presents today complaining of difficulty swallowing. He has noticed this over the last 4 to 5 weeks. He describes it as something being stuck in his throat and he has to wash it down on occasion. He denies ever fully choking but admits that he has thought about potentially choking. The patient notes that the sensation is more pronounced when he swallows solids, such as a bite of a sandwich, rather than liquids. He denies any weight loss or changes in his weight at all.

The patient reports that he has not noticed any blood in his stools or vomit. He denies chest pain or shortness of breath with this symptom.

The patient reports that he is doing well with his diabetes. He states that he is taking his metformin as prescribed and feels good otherwise. He notes that he checks his blood sugars about 80% of the time, but admits to skipping it occasionally when he is in a hurry. His blood sugar numbers are within the target range.

The patient reports that he is doing well with his blood pressure. He states that his blood pressure looks good at home, but notes that it can be higher on occasion.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or shortness of breath.
• Gastrointestinal: Denies hematemesis, melena, abdominal pain.
• Endocrine: Reports improved diabetes control.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: Supple without swelling or masses; normal thyroid examination; no carotid bruit.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Hemoglobin A1c: 7.4
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Difficulty swallowing.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with esophageal narrowing or stricture causing dysphagia.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed the nature of the patient's symptoms and recommended dietary modifications to help prevent food from getting stuck in the esophagus and also recommended Prilosec for potential gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) symptoms which can exacerbate dysphagia.
- Additional Testing and Treatment Plan: I have referred the patient for gastroenterology for further evaluation and treatment of his dysphagia via endoscopy and dilation if necessary.
2. Diabetes Type 2.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's hemoglobin A1c was last checked at 7.4%, which is within target range on metformin 500 mg twice daily, but we will repeat this test today to confirm stability of blood sugar control.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed dietary modifications with the patient to help improve glycemic control, but we will continue to monitor him closely for any changes in blood sugar levels.
- Additional Testing and Treatment Plan: Repeat hemoglobin A1c ordered today; continue metformin as prescribed; refer for ophthalmology for diabetic eye exam due to diabetes status.
3. Hypertension Type 2.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's current blood pressure was noted to be within target range in office today, however we will continue to monitor him closely for any changes in blood pressure levels at home.

Mr. Jerry Cook is a 45-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right ankle pain and instability. He describes the pain as being on the outside of his ankle, which is bruised up and swollen. He notes that he has been having trouble walking due to the pain and instability in his right ankle.

The patient reports that he recently resumed engaging in a consistent gym routine, but he does not want to disrupt this due to his current symptoms.

PAST HISTORY

Skin: Reports right ankle bruising and swelling.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Lateral malleolar fracture.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Michelle King is a 44-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of her symptoms began when she was skiing in Vermont last weekend. She was coming off the lift when she caught her ski and fell, resulting in her knee popping. She was unable to bear weight and was taken down by the ski patrol. She reports that she has been experiencing pain on the lateral aspect of her knee, as well as difficulty bearing weight. She denies any numbness or tingling in her toes.

The patient is a very active individual who enjoys skiing and taking care of her 4-year-old twins. Her husband works a job where he is gone quite a bit, so it is just her and the kids at home. She reports that she has been hobbling around on crutches at home due to her current symptoms.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Reports she is otherwise healthy and denies a history of high blood pressure or diabetes.
Social: Very active with skiing and taking care of her 4-year-old twins. Her husband works a job where he is gone quite a bit.
MEDICATIONS

Ibuprofen.
ALLERGIES

No known allergies.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Right knee pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient sustained an injury to her right ACL during skiing last weekend. The x-ray did not show any bony abnormalities but we are concerned that she has ruptured her ACL. We have ordered a MRI for further evaluation.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options with the patient today including continuing ibuprofen as needed, wearing a brace for support, and waiting for the MRI results before proceeding with further treatment options such as surgery or physical therapy.
- Medical Treatment: Continue ibuprofen 600-800 mg every 8 hours as needed for pain control. Wear a brace for support at home until we receive the MRI results back.

Neck pain.

The patient reports that he was involved in 4 motor vehicle accidents.

The patient reports that he is married.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Yearly exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Beverly Ortiz is a 24-year-old female who presents for her yearly exam. She has a history of type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure. She has been working at a bakery this summer, which has been super fun. However, she finds herself snacking a lot during shifts and eating more desserts than she normally would.

Her blood sugars have been up and down because of her diet, she thinks, as she has not missed any of her prescribed medication. Her diet has been pretty bad lately.

Her blood pressure has been good despite her diabetes levels being up and down. She is sleeping well and denies any concerns about hurting herself or anything like that.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Endocrine: Reports elevated hemoglobin A1c.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
• Neurological: Denies headaches or dizziness.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. Grade 2 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left sternal border. No murmurs at the axilla or pulmonary area. No gallops, rales, or rubs.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Hemoglobin A1c is elevated.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
- Medical Reasoning: Elevated hemoglobin A1c levels indicate that her blood glucose levels have been elevated over time. Her diet has likely contributed to this issue.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed dietary changes that may help improve her blood glucose levels. I advised her to cut down on snacking and additional sweets.
- Medical Treatment: Her current medication regimen remains unchanged at this time.
- Additional Testing: We will check her morning fasting blood sugar in 2 weeks to see if there are any improvements in her blood glucose levels.
- Special Testing: Repeat hemoglobin A1c in 2 months if there are no improvements in her blood glucose levels.
2. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: Her blood pressure has been stable on lisinopril 10 mg once daily.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of adhering to her current medication regimen as prescribed.
- Medical Treatment: Continue lisinopril 10 mg once daily as prescribed.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

High blood pressure.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Susan Watson is a 26-year-old female who presents for a high blood pressure check. She has struggled with high blood pressure for some time, but it has been getting out of control lately. She is currently taking Norvasc 10 mg daily and her blood pressures have been running over 150 at home. She denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or any other symptoms.

The patient reports that she has had headaches, which she believes may be related to her high blood pressure or stress at work.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that she underwent a kidney transplant a few years ago. She denies any issues with the transplant.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that she is taking all of her immunosuppression medications.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Cardiovascular: Reports headaches.
• Neurological: Reports headaches.

• Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezes, rales, or rhonchi.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. High Blood Pressure.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood pressure is elevated despite being on Norvasc 10 mg daily. Her kidney function looks good after her transplant and there are no other obvious causes for her elevated blood pressure at this time.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications and medical treatment options in detail today.
- Medical Treatment: We discussed the benefits and risks of Coreg 25 mg twice daily in addition to Norvasc 10 mg daily. I have prescribed Coreg 25 mg twice daily in addition to Norvasc 10 mg daily. I also recommended that we obtain a lipid panel and routine labs to ensure everything looks good from a transplant standpoint.
- Additional Testing: Lipid panel and complete metabolic panel ordered.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mrs. Lee is a 40-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of back pain. The onset of her pain began at a birthday party when she was surprised by her friends and family. She was hiding behind others and then jumped out when the person came in, causing her to fall down the stairs and ramming her back into the railing of the staircase. She reports that she thinks she twisted while jumping up from the fall. The patient denies any pain shooting down her legs. Her pain is more on the right side of her back. She notes that lying flat hurts a little more, and any twisting motion makes it worse.

The patient reports that she has a history of lumbar fusion.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right-sided back pain.
Neurological: Denies lower extremity pain or numbness.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal: Examination of the spine reveals no evidence of acute trauma or deformity. There is some stiffness with rotation, but no evidence of radiculopathy or pinched nerve.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray examination reveals T4 fusion in place.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Strain of lower back.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient sustained an injury to her lower back when she was twisting at the birthday party. She does not have any evidence of acute trauma or deformity on examination, but does have some stiffness with rotation.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options today, including continuing Motrin 800mg 3 times daily with food, using ice and heat alternating on her back, and walking as much as possible.
- Medical Treatment: Continue Motrin 800mg 3 times daily with food. Use ice and heat alternating on her back. Encourage walking as much as possible.
- Additional Testing: X-ray examination was performed today which revealed T4 fusion in place without any evidence of compression fractures or other abnormalities.
