note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Rebecca Thompson is a 27-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of her symptoms began 1 month ago when she started swimming more regularly. She has been trying to get up and get active. She uses the breaststroke so she guesses where the legs are kicking out like a frog. It kinda starts hurting a little bit after she swims a couple laps, which a month ago when she started she was able to do ten laps without any issues.

The patient denies any history of injury.

The patient reports that her chronic back pain has been doing well, but she does experience some discomfort at times. She denies any lower extremity pain or weakness.

The patient reports that her depression has been stable with medication and therapy, and that it has been helping her. She denies any suicidal ideation or plans.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
Neurological: Denies lower extremity weakness or numbness.
Psychiatric: Reports stable depression.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Examination of the right knee: No swelling in the joint. There is some pain with range of motion of the knee. There is patellar inhibition, which is causing most of the pain.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee was reviewed in office today and shows no evidence of fracture or dislocation. The x-ray is otherwise unremarkable.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Chondromalacia of the patella.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms began 1 month ago when she started swimming more regularly. She uses the breaststroke so she guesses where the legs are kicking out like a frog. It kinda starts hurting a little bit after she swims a couple laps, which a month ago when she started she was able to do ten laps without any issues.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed with her today that this is likely due to overuse from swimming and that we will treat this conservatively with anti-inflammatories, ibuprofen 600 mg four times daily with food, as well as straight leg raising exercises to strengthen her quadriceps muscle.
- Medical Treatment: We will start anti-inflammatories today and have her follow up in 2 weeks if her symptoms do not improve.
2. Chronic back pain.
- Medical Reasoning: Her chronic back pain has been doing well lately but we discussed that if it flares up again we should contact us for further evaluation and treatment options.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed with her today that we want her to continue swimming as long as possible until this improves, but avoid anything that puts extra pressure on her knees for now until it improves.
- Medical Treatment: Continue as usual.

Resistant hypertension.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Jordan Roberts is a 49-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of resistant hypertension. He reports that he has been experiencing high blood pressure since he was young. He notes that his blood pressure has been elevated at home, with readings ranging from 146-155 mmHg. He denies any episodes of palpitations since his last visit to the emergency room in March.

The patient reports that he was recently in the emergency room with high blood pressure and some palpitations. He believes that this was likely due to a panic attack.

The patient is currently taking Benicar HCT 40 mg/25 mg and Amlodipine 10 mg daily. He notes that his potassium level was 4.0 mg/dL one week ago, which is within the normal range.

The patient denies any changes in his diet or exercise habits, but notes that he has been trying to reduce his salt intake.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a family history of hypertension.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he is married and lives with his girlfriend.

RESULTS

Thyroid profile from 03/01/2021: Normal
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Mr. Jordan Roberts is a 49-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of resistant hypertension.

Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood pressure remains elevated despite being on maximum dose medication, which suggests resistant hypertension. His potassium level was normal at 4.0 mg/dL one week ago, which suggests that there may not be an electrolyte imbalance contributing to his elevated blood pressure.
Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of reducing salt intake and increasing potassium levels in order to lower blood pressure. I also provided him with information on the DASH eating plan and recommended that he check out the American Heart Association website for more information on how to control his diet with exercise.
Medical Treatment: We have added spironolactone to his regimen today, as it has been shown to be effective in lowering aldosterone levels and blood pressure in patients with resistant hypertension. We will need to monitor his potassium and sodium levels closely while on this medication.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.
Next Office Visit: We will schedule a follow-up appointment in two weeks to check on his blood pressure and electrolyte levels.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) with functional abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Brittany Edwards is a pleasant 32-year-old female who presents for a return visit for IBS with functional abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She was last seen in August 2019 with flares of abdominal pain, who was diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome that was treated with Bentyl.

The patient reports that she has been going out to eat on Friday nights and Saturdays and has had some spicy foods or spicy shrimp. She denies that her gut likes it at all. The patient states that she is starting to notice that she is having bowel movements between 2-3 times a day on normal days. Her stools are described as formed. She reports that after she has gone out drinking with friends, she tends to have more diarrhea. The patient feels it is the food or alcohol or both.

She notes that she usually eats pasta at Fridays restaurant and the chicken alfredo sauce does not bother her normally. However, pasta can make her bloated but does not usually cause diarrhea. Grilled chicken is usually okay but the alfredo sauce contains dairy which may be contributing to her symptoms.

The patient states that most of the time she drinks tequila or dark liquor when eating out and prefers Patron but will only have 2 if she gets brown liquor. Occasionally, she will drink a martini.

She denies using the fiber supplement Citrucel regularly as prescribed by her previous provider. She states that she needs to find a new drink.

Her symptoms have been present during the week as well as on weekends when she eats out and drinks alcohol.

The patient reports that right now, she is still having cramping and sharp pains so has been avoiding heavy foods. She did have some fried chicken today though and everything was alright after that.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• General Examination: The patient is alert and cooperative in appearance stated age.
• Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm.
• Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Brittany Edwards is a pleasant female with IBS with functional abdominal pain aggravated by high stress, poor eating habits, and poor sleeping habits.
• Medical Reasoning: Her symptoms are consistent with IBS which can be exacerbated by dietary triggers such as spicy foods or fatty foods as well as stress.
• Patient Education and Counseling: I encouraged dietary modifications such as avoiding greasy or fatty foods and sugary drinks as well as reducing alcohol consumption. We discussed neuromodulators such as Elavil 25 mg at bedtime for IBS treatment options.
• Medical Treatment: We discussed starting Citrucel twice daily for regularity. If we know you are going out and will possibly have diarrhea as a result, you can go ahead and use Bentyl 20 mg up to four times daily before eating out at a restaurant. You can do one tablet before you eat, then repeat up to four times daily on days when you feel good you do not have to use anything. On Fridays before leaving the house take one Bentyl tablet put one in your pocket for later then repeat same thing on Saturdays if you want this will be totally fine.
• Additional Testing: None today.
• Special Tests: None today.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Adult hydrocephalus.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Christopher Watson is an 86-year-old male who returns in follow-up for adult hydrocephalus. This is his first visit since undergoing shunt surgery on August 1st, 2020.

The patient was status post shunt placement on August 1st, 2020, with a Medtronic Strata programmable shunt in the ventricular peritoneal configuration placed at level 2.0.

Prior to surgery, the patient was experiencing progressive problems that affected his walking, thinking, and bladder control. These symptoms have improved since the surgery. He is now able to walk to the dining room just fine but still requires assistance at times. His bladder control has also improved but has leveled out and he is currently wearing diapers without any issues with sores or decreased or painful urination.

The patient reports that he feels better and does not feel lost when talking to someone anymore. He notes that he can have a normal conversation with him again.

He denies any headaches or pain where the shunt is and denies any pain in his belly.

The patient states that he has not been sick or hospitalized since his shunt surgery three months ago.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever or unintentional weight loss.
• Genitourinary: Reports urinary incontinence and wearing a diaper.
• Neurological: Reports continued walking impairment and cognitive impairment. Denies headaches, recent falls, or hallucinations.
• Psychiatric: Denies depression, excessive worrying, or mood swings.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Constitutional: Rosenthalian appearance for age in weight and height. Negative for fever or unintentional weight loss.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• CT scan of the head from 10/15/2020 shows frontal horn span at the level of foramen of Munro of 4.6 cm with third ventricular contour flat with span of 10 mm. There is substantial small vessel ischemic change.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Adult hydrocephalus.
Gait impairment.
Urinary incontinence and urgency.
Cognitive impairment.

His bladder control has also improved but has leveled out and he is currently wearing diapers without any issues with sores or decreased or painful urination.
Medical Treatment: We will continue to monitor him closely over the next two to three months before we go in changing his shunt again if necessary.

Ms. Ross denies any history of irregular Pap smears, but she did have an abnormal Pap smear around the age of 20. Her last Pap smear was approximately 6 months ago and was normal.

note.objective_exam:

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Tyler Nelson is a 72-year-old male who presents for ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis. Last time he was seen, he received a steroid injection in his right knee on 03/04/2021. He reports that the injection did not help, as his knee is still swollen and painful. He notes that the pain level is about a 3 out of 10, but typically it is around 6 on a normal day. The swelling has been present for approximately 2 months now, and it was not present before that time. He has been wearing compression socks to try to help with the swelling, but they have not been helpful.

The patient reports that the swelling has been keeping him from doing things during the day. He notes that when he sits for a while, he gets stiff and has difficulty getting up without using a cane to get his bearings. However, after a little while, the stiffness loosens up.

The patient reports that he has been taking his Xeljanz XR 11 mg daily and Celebrex 200 mg daily as prescribed by his primary care physician. He notes that the Celebrex started working well until he began to experience swelling again.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain and swelling.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MSK: Examination of the right knee reveals decreased range of motion with pain upon full extension. There is edema over the lateral aspect of the knee and ankle with capillary refill in the toes.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Fluid aspiration and steroid injection procedure performed today.
Risks, benefits, and alternatives were explained.
Verbal consent was obtained.
The right knee was accessed through the lateral approach with 3 mL of initially clear fluid, then blood-tinged fluid.
Right knee was prepped in standard fashion.
Right knee injected with 80 mg triamcinolone and 1 mL lidocaine.
The procedure was tolerated well with no complications post-procedure instructions were given.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis.
- Continue Xeljanz XR 11 mg daily as prescribed by primary care physician.
- Continue Celebrex 200 mg daily as prescribed by primary care physician.
- Limit salt intake to reduce edema.
- Elevate legs at night to reduce edema.
- Physical therapy recommended for right knee due to decreased range of motion and pain upon full extension.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Perioral dermatitis, rosacea, including ocular rosacea.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jacqueline Miller is a 40-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for a follow-up examination. She was previously seen on for perioral dermatitis, rosacea, including ocular rosacea. At that time, she was using doxycycline cream twice daily and MetroCream once daily. She noticed improvement with the doxycycline cream but plateaued when she switched to once daily. She stopped breastfeeding and started using doxycycline cream at that time. She has been using MetroCream once daily and sulfacetamide wash twice daily.

The patient reports that her symptoms have not improved with the current treatment regimen. She denies any new medications or products being added to her routine.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Skin: Denies any new skin lesions or rashes.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Fitzpatrick skin type IV.
Bilateral medial cheeks: There are a few faint erythematous papules and just a little bit of redness around and underneath the nostrils.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Perioral dermatitis, rosacea, including ocular rosacea.
Copy and paste her patient instructions.
I reviewed the patient's exam in detail today. We discussed her current treatment regimen in length at length today. I recommended that she increase her use of doxycycline cream to twice daily until her rash resolves, then decrease to once daily for 1 week before stopping. I also recommended that she resume using Elidel cream as well as continue with MetroCream and sulfacetamide wash as usual. We discussed the risks associated with Elidel cream in detail today and I explained that it is generally considered safe when used topically in as-needed fashion without immunosuppression.
I also recommended that she use Vanicream gentle cleanser once a day on her eyelids as well as Bruder mask as needed for ocular rosacea.
We will follow up in 4 weeks.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right upper quadrant pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Michael Rodriguez is a 47-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right upper quadrant pain. The onset of his pain began several weeks ago and has been intermittent in nature. He describes the pain as severe and localized to the right side of his abdomen, just below his right ribs. The pain is described as a squeezing type of pain that comes and goes, but when it does, it is very severe. He reports nausea and vomiting with his pain.

The patient reports that he has noticed an improvement in his symptoms with dietary modifications. He notes that he has cut back on sugar and started a keto diet, which has resulted in weight loss of 25 pounds over the last 3 months. His blood sugars have also improved since he started making these dietary changes.

The patient denies any fevers or vomiting associated with his symptoms.

PAST HISTORY

Medical History: Type 2 diabetes managed with diet and exercise.
Social History: Enjoys nature photography.
Family History: Family history of cholelithiasis. Both parents have had cholecystectomies.
Medications: Currently managing type 2 diabetes with diet and exercise.
Allergies: None reported.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS
- Blood Pressure: 128/88 mmHg
- Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths per minute
- Heart Rate: 68 beats per minute
- Oxygen Saturation: 99% on room air
- Body Temperature: Afebrile
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Abdominal ultrasound obtained at an outside facility shows multiple gallstones present in the gallbladder with some mild thickening. The common bile duct size is within normal limits at 4.1 mm.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Michael Rodriguez is a 47-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right upper quadrant pain.
1. Medical Reasoning:
• The patient's ultrasound shows multiple gallstones present in the gallbladder with some mild thickening. This is consistent with mild cholecystitis due to gallstones.
• The patient's symptoms have not improved with dietary modifications alone, which suggests that he will require surgical intervention to remove his gallbladder.
2. Patient Education and Counseling:
• We discussed the risks and benefits of laparoscopic cholecystectomy today in detail.
• We discussed post-operative care including avoiding high fat foods for several weeks after surgery, eating foods high in fiber, and taking it easy for the first 24 hours after surgery.
• We discussed follow-up care including seeing me again in one week to remove any sutures and then follow up as needed after that time period.
3. Medical Treatment Plan:
• Surgical Intervention: I am recommending that we proceed with a laparoscopic cholecystectomy today to remove his gallbladder.

He reports that his right knee feels 95% improved since his total knee arthroplasty in the spring of 2020.

The patient states that he has been taking Tylenol and Ibuprofen for pain relief, but they have not been effective. He has tried heat and ice, but they have not helped either. He denies any stomach upset from the Ibuprofen.

PAST HISTORY

Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Teresa Sullivan is a 33-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right elbow pain. The onset of her pain began 4 days ago. She reports that her pain is located on the medial aspect of her right elbow. She denies any history of trauma to the area. The patient has been engaging in pottery and baking, which she states has been causing her pain. She rates her pain level as a 7/10 at its worst. The patient reports that she has not been able to work on her pottery due to the pain.

The patient denies any radiation of pain down her arm or up to her shoulder. She does report that she has noticed some improvement with ice application, but it has not been effective in relieving her symptoms.

The patient reports that she has been taking ibuprofen, but it has not provided any relief for her symptoms.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of hypertension and diabetes type 2.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol in moderation.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that she is currently taking lisinopril 10 mg daily and metformin 500 mg twice daily.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Cardiovascular: No murmurs, gallops, or rubs were heard. Lungs are clear bilaterally to auscultation.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right Elbow Pain.
- Medical Reasoning: This appears to be consistent with medial epicondylitis.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the nature of medial epicondylitis and how it can be caused by overuse and damage to the tendons in your arm.
- Medical Treatment: We will start you on a sling for your right arm today. I am going to order an ice pack for you to apply 20 minutes, 3 times per day. I am also going to prescribe 600 mg of ibuprofen, taken every 6 hours with food, for one week. We will hold off on pottery for the next couple of weeks until your arm heals.
- Additional Testing: X-ray was reviewed today in office and appears normal with no evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.
- Additional Treatment: We will consider physical therapy if this does not improve within a couple of weeks.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Gregory Price is a 68-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of his symptoms began 2.5 weeks ago when he stepped off a curb and turned his right ankle to the outside. He denies any actual fall but states that he thought his ankle was going to be the most painful part of the injury. After the initial ankle soreness resolved, he noticed that his knee was sore and would click when he walks. He denies any pain with ambulation but notes that when he stands on one foot for an extended period, such as leaning against a wall, he feels like his knee is locked and has to ease into walking again.

The patient reports that he has been taking ibuprofen for pain relief but notes that it does not impact his symptoms during the day as he works through it. However, at night, it does help him to settle down and sleep better.

The patient states that his knee is fine when it is elevated but becomes painful when he rests it on his heel. He denies any pain with rest or sitting.

He reports that he is able to perform a full squat without any pain but notes that this is when he feels the most clicking in his knee. He denies any numbness or tingling in his foot at all.

The patient reports that he has broken his 2nd toe on his right foot 3 times over the last 10 years and notes that this is an annoyance but not caused by this current injury.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left lower extremity pain.
Neurological: Reports numbness in right foot.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal Examination of the Right Knee: There is slight edema over the lateral aspect of the knee. There is effusion present bilaterally. Palpation of the lateral aspect of the right knee reveals no pain with palpation. Varus testing reveals a positive test bilaterally, full ROM bilaterally, and negative Lachman sign.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee was reviewed in office today and does not show any acute fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Mr. Gregory Price is a 68-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of right knee pain.
1) Medical Reasoning: The patient's examination findings are consistent with a lateral collateral ligament strain.
2) Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed treatment options with him today including conservative management with meloxicam 15 mg once daily and referral to physical therapy for strengthening exercises around the injured area.
3) Medical Treatment: I have prescribed meloxicam 15 mg once daily for treatment of lateral collateral ligament strain.
4) Additional Testing: We will refer him to physical therapy if symptoms do not improve with conservative management.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right heel pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Dennis Martin is a 46-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right heel pain. The onset of his symptoms began 10 days ago. He reports that his pain is located in the posterior aspect of his heel, radiating proximally into the calf. His pain is aggravated by working out and when he first gets up in the morning. He notes that he runs 10 kilometers in the morning, bikes for 45 minutes to an hour at lunchtime, and swims for 30 minutes to an hour in the evening. He trains 5 days per week and alternates between a long run and a long bike ride on weekends. He does not stretch at all.

The patient reports that his pain typically begins after he has completed his workout or when he first gets up in the morning. It will often hurt all the way up into his calf. He notes that after he has been walking around for about 10-15 minutes, it will ease up a bit but if he sits down for any extended period of time and then tries to get back up, it will be sore again.

The patient also reports that after a lot of activity, his pain will get sore as well.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right heel pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MSK: Examination of lower extremities reveals no left leg pain. The patient's right leg is tender to palpation over the plantar fascia bilaterally but more so on the right side. The patient's Achilles tendon is tender to palpation bilaterally but more so on the right side.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Dennis Martin is a 46-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right heel pain.

Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with Achilles tendinitis due to overuse.
Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed with him what we discussed today and have advised him to stop training for a week or two until we see improvement in his symptoms.
Additional Testing: We did not order any additional testing today as we feel that this diagnosis can be made based on clinical examination alone at this time.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.
Medical Treatment Plan: We have started him on ibuprofen 3 tablets every 6 hours as needed for anti-inflammatory purposes. I have also ordered physical therapy visits to help strengthen his lower extremities as well as teach him proper stretching techniques before starting these activities again. I would like him to follow up with me within 1 week to 10 days following his first couple physical therapy appointments so we can monitor how he is doing.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Non-healing right foot ulcer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Christina Cooper is a 77-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer. The patient reports that she has had this ulcer for approximately 1 year. She denies any trauma to the foot, but states that she developed a blister and then picked at it, which became infected. She was treated with antibiotics, which seemed to improve her symptoms initially, but they have not resolved. The patient reports that her foot does not hurt, but she does not have sensation in her foot. She also reports increased drainage from the ulcer and fatigue.

The patient’s diabetes is well-controlled with insulin and metformin. Her last hemoglobin A1c was 10, which is elevated. She will follow up with her primary care provider regarding this.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever or chills.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies pain in the right foot.
• Neurological: Reports decreased sensation in the right foot.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Skin Examination: There is a 1 x 2 cm circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot proximal to the 5th MTP joint. There is yellow slough present with minimal granulation tissue. There is no surrounding erythema or cellulitis and there is no evidence of fluid collection. There is no necrosis or odor present. I do not appreciate any bony exposure.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right foot was performed prior to today’s visit and showed no evidence of osteomyelitis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Christina Cooper is a 77-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient’s diabetic foot ulcer appears to be non-healing despite treatment with antibiotics and debridement in office previously.
• Additional Testing: We will order an ABI (ankle brachial index) today to assess blood flow to her feet.
• Medical Treatment: We will perform debridement in office today and prescribe colaganase ointment for application once daily until we see improvement in size of the wound.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed dietary modifications with regards to diabetes management today.
• Additional Testing Ordered: ABI (ankle brachial index)
• Medical Treatment Ordered: Debridement in office today; colaganase ointment prescribed for application once daily until we see improvement in size of wound; surgical shoe prescribed.

Lives with dog. San Francisco 49ers fan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Abdominal pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Barbara White is a 31-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of abdominal pain. The onset of her pain began 1 week ago. She reports that she has been drinking a lot of coffee lately and believes that this may have triggered her gastritis. She denies fever with her pain. Her nausea and vomiting are intermittent, occurring 3 times per week. She notes that her abdominal pain is worse when she exercises, such as jogging or running. She denies any weight loss or changes in bowel habits.

Ms. White reports that she has a history of diabetes type 2 and asthma, for which she is currently taking metformin 500 mg twice daily and Flovent twice daily as needed for wheezing.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fevers.
• Gastrointestinal: Reports nausea and vomiting on and off.
• Respiratory: Reports wheezing.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Cardiovascular: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur at the left sternal border unchanged from prior exam.
• Respiratory: Mild end-expiratory wheezes bilaterally, otherwise normal lung exam with excellent air movement.
• Abdomen: Mild tenderness in the epigastrium, otherwise soft. No tenderness in the right lower quadrant or right upper quadrant.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Acute gastritis.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with acute gastritis, likely related to caffeine intake and moderately heavy alcohol use. Her history of diabetes type 2 is also present but does not appear to be contributing to her current symptoms.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised the patient to cut back on alcohol consumption to less than 2-3 drinks per week and reduce caffeine intake as well. I also recommended cutting back on spicy foods as well.
- Medical Treatment: I have prescribed Zantac for symptom relief.
- Additional Testing: Urinalysis, urine pregnancy test, CBC, comprehensive metabolic panel will be ordered to rule out other causes of her symptoms.

2. Diabetes Type 2.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood glucose levels have been under control with metformin 500 mg twice daily but we will increase this dose to 1000 mg once daily in the morning and keep it at 500 mg once daily in the evening due to her last visit we increased this dose from what was prescribed initially so we will continue with that regimen going forward.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised the patient to continue checking her blood glucose levels when she comes back in for follow up in 4 weeks.
- Medical Treatment: Continue metformin as prescribed above.

3. Asthma.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's asthma appears to be well controlled with Flovent twice daily as needed for wheezing; however, she has not had any recent asthma attacks so we will continue with this regimen going forward if she continues without any issues.

Right elbow pain.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of hypertension and diabetes.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he plays lacrosse with his children.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that he is currently taking Lisinopril 20 mg daily and Metformin 500 mg daily.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right elbow pain.
Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
Gastrointestinal: Denies abdominal pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

CV: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, heard at the left sternal border.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-ray of the right elbow was obtained today and reviewed in office. There is no evidence of a fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right elbow contusion.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient sustained an injury to his right elbow when he was hit by a lacrosse stick while playing with his children. This resulted in swelling, inflammation, and bruising in the olecranon area of the posterior elbow. His x-ray shows no evidence of a fracture or bony abnormality.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options for his current symptoms, including rest, ice, compression, elevation (RICE), and anti-inflammatory medication (ibuprofen). We also advised him to avoid playing lacrosse with his son for the next couple of weeks to allow time for healing.
- Medical Treatment: I have prescribed 800 mg ibuprofen twice daily for pain management. I have also advised him to ice it 3 times per day for 20 minutes at a time to help reduce swelling and pain.
2. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: His blood pressure was elevated at 150/90 mmHg today, but this appears to be white coat hypertension given that he has been compliant with his medication regimen and dietary modifications as recommended by me previously.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications that can help lower blood pressure, including dietary changes (low sodium) and regular exercise (e.g., walking). We also reviewed medication adherence as well as any potential side effects associated with lisinopril use.
- Medical Treatment: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily as prescribed. Continue dietary modifications as previously recommended.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Acute on chronic congestive heart failure.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. James Davis is an 82-year-old male with past medical history significant for hypertension and stage 3 chronic kidney disease who presents for hospital follow-up after an acute on chronic chf exacerbation. He reports that he has been trying to watch his diet as recommended by the physician, but he noticed that his ankles were swelling. He also noticed that he was getting really short of breath and he even had to call 911. When the paramedics arrived, they put him on the special mask to breathe. When he got to the ER, the doctor in the ER said his blood pressure was super high.

The patient denies chest pain since he has been home.

The patient reports that he has been taking his medications most of the time, but sometimes he misses a dose or two. He states that he really tries to take them for the most part.

PAST HISTORY

Medical History: Hypertension and stage 3 chronic kidney disease.
Social History: Football fan.

MEDICATIONS

Bumex 2 mg once daily; Cozaar 100 mg daily; Norvasc 5 mg once daily.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No jugular venous distention.
Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur stable.
Respiratory: Clear bilaterally. No wheezes or rales heard at auscultation of Lungs bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Echocardiogram shows preserved EF of 55% abnormal diastolic filling and mild to moderate mitral regurgitation.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Acute on chronic congestive heart failure.
- Medical Reasoning: This was caused by dietary indiscretion in uncontrolled hypertension.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed dietary modifications and avoiding salty foods such as pizza and chicken wings. I also recommended that we see a nutritionist for further education on healthy eating options.
- Medical Treatment: Continue Bumex 2 mg once daily; continue watching diet and avoid salty foods; weight self every day if gain more than 3 pounds in two days; refer to nutritionist for education on healthy eating options.
2. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: Continue Cozaar 100 mg daily and Norvasc 5 mg once daily, order renal artery ultrasound to rule out secondary causes of kidney disease.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications such as diet and exercise, but we will also order a renal artery ultrasound to rule out secondary causes of kidney disease.
- Medical Treatment: Continue Cozaar 100 mg daily; continue Norvasc 5 mg once daily; order renal artery ultrasound.
3. Stage 3 chronic kidney disease.
- Medical Reasoning: We will obtain additional labs to monitor tolerance of current regimen.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications such as diet and exercise, but we will also obtain additional labs to monitor tolerance of current regimen.
- Medical Treatment: Obtain additional labs.

Right ankle sprain.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Elevated cholesterol.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julie Cruz is a 17-year-old non-binary imminesipated minor with no significant past medical history. She presents for evaluation of newly diagnosed hypercholesterolemia. The patient is here at the clinic today because she was told that her cholesterol level was elevated at her annual checkup and she would like to have it checked again.

The patient reports that she enjoys being outside and riding her bike on trails. She states that she tries to eat a clean diet most days, but admits to enjoying chocolate chip cookies. She denies any history of hypercholesterolemia or anemia at an early age, but notes that her grandparents had a cousin who died of a heart attack in their 40s. The patient reports that her grandparents had their cholesterol levels checked last year and were told they were borderline, but they were advised to watch their diet.

The patient denies any issues with growing up, stating that she feels like she is growing normally. She also states that she has been living as a non-binary individual for about 2 years and feels healthy.

The patient reports that when she lived with her parents, they smoked, but she lives alone now and does not smoke. She also denies smoking when spending time with friends.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• General Examination: Vitality is good in appearance. No signs of distress or acute illness.
• Cardiovascular: No murmurs, gallops, or rubs heard in all 6 auscultation areas.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Cholesterol level: Elevated at 210
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Elevated cholesterol.
• Medical Reasoning: The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends screening children between the ages of 9-11 and again between the ages of 17-20 for elevated cholesterol levels due to studies showing a link between high cholesterol and premature heart attacks.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of dietary changes to help achieve healthy cholesterol levels. I recommended that we follow up in 3-6 months after meeting with a nutritionist who can provide guidance on what foods to eat.
• Additional Testing: Full cholesterol panel, glucose test, complete metabolic panel, thyroid studies, liver panels, and genetic testing will be ordered to determine if this is familial or secondary in nature.
• Medical Treatment: Dietary modifications will be implemented as recommended by the nutritionist.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Bilateral knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Sophia Jackson is a 30-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of bilateral knee pain. The onset of her symptoms began approximately 6 months ago. She denies any specific event that caused the onset of her pain. She describes her pain as a deep achy pain located behind her patella. She notes that she can hear creaking in her knees when she moves. Her pain is worse with ambulation from a seated position, stair climbing, and watching TV. Her pain improves with rest.

The patient reports that she has tried ice and compression bandages in the past. She also takes ibuprofen or Aleve as needed but tries to avoid taking any medications due to side effects. She notes that she has decreased her running distance significantly due to her knee pain.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of an upper extremity fracture when she was in 6th grade.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she works from home and is active, running 5-6 miles per day, but has had to decrease this significantly due to her knee pain.

MEDICATIONS AND SUPPLEMENTS

The patient reports taking ibuprofen and Aleve as needed.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS: All vital signs are within normal limits.
NEURO: Patellar and Achilles reflexes are symmetrical.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-rays of bilateral knees were obtained today and reviewed in office today. There are no fractures or osteoarthritis present.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Bilateral patellofemoral pain syndrome.
1. Medical Treatment: Continue taking ibuprofen or anti-inflammatory medication as needed for symptom management.
2. Physical Therapy: We will refer the patient for physical therapy to address lower extremity strength, mobility, and correct any incorrect running mechanics.
3. Activity Modification: We will continue to monitor the patient's progress with each visit while she continues to take it easy from running until we see improvement in her symptoms.
4. Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the nature of patellofemoral pain syndrome, its treatment options, and lifestyle modifications that may help alleviate symptoms.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Lumbar back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kyle Morales is a 58-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of lumbar back pain. The onset of his pain began 2 weeks ago when he was lifting a box of books. He denies any history of smoking. He reports that his pain is achy and sharp in nature, initially localized to his low back but now radiates down his left leg. He denies any numbness, tingling, or weakness associated with his pain. He also denies any loss of bladder or bowel control.

The patient reports that he has tried taking ibuprofen and Tylenol, which sometimes helps with his pain. He has not had any previous discussions with anyone about surgery.

The patient reports that he is an Olympic weightlifter and exercises a few times a week but is inconsistent due to a sedentary job. His job does not seem to be affected by his current symptoms.

He notes that his father has back pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports low back pain.
Neurological: Denies numbness, tingling, weakness, or loss of sensation.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Vitals: Blood pressure 130/70 mmHg; Respiratory rate 18.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, gallops, or rubs.
Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: Midline tenderness at L4-L5 disk space with right-sided lumbar paravertebral tenderness. Pain with lumbar flexion.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

MRI of the lumbar spine reveals disc desiccation and a disc bulge with paracentral disc herniation resulting in moderate right neuroforaminal stenosis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Lumbar back pain due to herniated disk with radiculopathy.
1) Medical Treatment: Continue ibuprofen and Tylenol as needed for symptom management.
2) Interventional Procedure: Spinal injection with corticosteroid and NSAID will be performed today in office under fluoroscopy to treat inflammation causing the patient's current symptoms.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Angela Powell is an 81-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of left knee pain. The onset of her pain began 1 week ago when she was running with her 5-year-old niece. She states that she twisted her knee and heard a pop. She rates her pain as a 4 out of 10 initially, but it has increased to a throbbing type of pain. She notes that she has been limping since the onset of her pain and it has not improved.

Ms. Powell reports that she has been taking Tylenol for her pain, but it only provides temporary relief. She notes that she cannot take ibuprofen due to a prior ulcer, but she can take Tylenol as needed for breakthrough pain. She also reports that she wrapped her knee with kinesiology tape.

PAST HISTORY

Patient reports a history of ulcer.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient reports running with her niece.

MEDICATIONS

Patient reports taking Tylenol.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left knee pain.
Neurological: Denies any neurological symptoms.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Left Knee Examination in Office Today.
• Examination: Examination of the left knee reveals effusion and edema. Range of motion is moderate, but not full range due to pain on flexion and extension. Negative Lachman's test and negative valgus and varus testing.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-rays of the left knee were obtained today and reviewed in office today. These are normal, showing no fractures or bony abnormalities.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN IN OFFICE TODAY.
Left Knee Pain.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient sustained an MCL strain when running with her niece, which is consistent with the nature of her symptoms and examination findings today.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the nature of her injury in detail today, including the importance of avoiding weight-bearing activities on the left leg for the next 3 weeks to allow for healing time. We also discussed ice therapy, immobilization, and medication options in detail today.
• Medical Treatment: We have placed the patient on tramadol 50 mg twice daily for pain management. We have also placed her in a knee immobilizer to keep the knee from moving while it heals. We have also recommended ice therapy 3-4 times per day for 20-30 minutes at a time to help reduce swelling. The patient will follow up with me in 1 week to re-evaluate.

Ms. Price is currently taking metformin 1000 mg daily and lisinopril. She reports that her diet has been great lately and she has been power walking every day. She checks her blood sugars in the morning and fasting blood sugars.

Ms. Price reports that her high blood pressure has been stable on medication and she is taking it every day. She also reports that she has been stable since her ACL repair 5 years ago.

note.objective_exam:

• Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally without wheezes or rales.
• Cardiovascular: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur at the left sternal border.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Hemoglobin A1c: Elevated at 8.1.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Diabetes Type 2.
- Medical Reasoning: Her hemoglobin A1c is elevated at 8.1 despite being on metformin 1000 mg daily. We should add Jardiance 10 mg daily to see if we can get her hemoglobin A1c down the next time.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised her to follow her diet aggressively to see if we can get that hemoglobin A1c down the next time.
- Medical Treatment: We will start Jardiance 10 mg daily today and order additional labs including a lipid panel today.
2. High Blood Pressure.
- Medical Reasoning: Her blood pressure is stable on lisinopril daily at home with a home cuff.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised her to continue monitoring her blood pressure at home as we will re-check it again next time.
- Medical Treatment: Continue lisinopril daily as prescribed.
3. Right ACL Repair.
- Medical Reasoning: She reports that she has not had any issues with mobility since surgery 5 years ago and continues with normal exercise regimen including power walking about 30 minutes per day.

He is planning to take a vacation in the new year. The patient reports that he has not been able to continue his morning long walks due to the cold weather and is looking for alternative options.

Regarding his depression, the patient states that he has not been ready to try any medications yet. He notes that he has been going for long walks outside every morning during the summer months. He also encourages himself to do some yard work on the weekends which was a nice way to be active and get some sun. However, with the changing seasons and it getting cold out, he has not been able to continue doing this and is looking into alternative options.

The patient denies any thoughts of harming himself or others.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Evaluating a 60-year-old male for numbness and tingling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

The patient is a 60-year-old right-handed male who presents today for the evaluation of numbness and tingling in both hands. He reports that he has been experiencing these symptoms for the past few weeks. The onset of his symptoms began after he broke his wrists in a motor vehicle accident in December 2019. He notes that his right wrist was in worse shape at the time of the injury, but he has been wearing a splint on both wrists since then. The patient states that his symptoms have worsened over the past month, with increased stiffness in his neck as well. He reports that he hit his head during the accident and was told it was a contusion.

The patient describes the nature of his pain as sore, with some throbbing, but overall, he feels weaker when using his hands. The tingling is more pronounced when it hurts, but when it resolves, the tingling is dull. He denies any loss of sensation in his hands or fingers, although he notes that they may be less sensitive than they should be.

The patient reports that his symptoms are worse at night and come and go throughout the day. He denies any pain or burning sensations when he is not experiencing pain or numbness.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Reports fatigue and weight gain.
Gastrointestinal: Reports excessive appetite and bloating.
Eyes: Reports floaters.
Cardiovascular: Reports shortness of breath and bilateral peripheral edema.
Endocrine: Reports always being hungry.
Skin: Reports dryness, itching, nail bed changes.
Musculoskeletal: Reports gout and muscle pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological Examination:
• Sensation: Decreased pin prick sensation in 3rd and 4th fingers on right side; decreased pin prick sensation in 4th and 5th fingers on left side.
• Reflexes: Normal to 1+ bilaterally; 2+ knees; downgoing toes bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• EMG testing will be ordered to determine if nerve irritation is present.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome or potentially bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptom presentation suggests bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome due to past trauma causing nerve irritation. His EMG testing will help determine if this is indeed present.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options with the patient today including EMG testing followed by referral to hand clinic for injections or carpal tunnel release surgery if necessary.
• Medical Treatment: We will order an EMG test to determine if nerve irritation is present. If positive, we will refer him to hand clinic for injections or carpal tunnel release surgery if necessary.

Bilateral hand numbness and tingling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kimberly Taylor is a 60-year-old right-handed female who presents for the evaluation of bilateral hand numbness and tingling. The onset of her symptoms began 2 weeks ago, after she broke her wrists in a motor vehicle accident. She notes that her symptoms have been worsening over the last month. She denies any pain, but reports that her hands feel weaker, especially when she is using them. The patient reports that she has noticed more tingling and numbness in her left hand compared to her right hand. She notes that the tingling is worse in her middle and ring fingers all the way up to her forearm on the right side, and on her left, it is worse in the pinky and ring fingers but not as much as on the right side.

The patient reports that she has been wearing a splint on both wrists, but only wears it on her left wrist sometimes. The splint seems to help with her symptoms. She denies any pain or burning sensation, but reports that when she does experience pain, it goes away and then the tingling returns.

The patient reports that she experiences bilateral hand numbness at night, which resolves throughout the day.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Reports fatigue and weight gain.
GI: Reports excessive appetite and bloating.
Eyes: Reports floaters.
Cardiovascular: Reports shortness of breath and leg swelling.
Endocrine: Positive diabetes, always hungry.
Skin: Reports nail bed trenches, dryness, itching.
Musculoskeletal: Reports gout, muscle pain.
Neurological: Reports parasthesia in bilateral hands.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological Examination:
• Sensations normal except pin prick sensation diminished in the 3rd and 4th fingers on the right side. Diminished pin prick sensation in the 4th and 5th fingers on the left side. Reflexes are 1+ bilaterally symmetric at knees. 2+ bilaterally down going toes bilaterally. Tinel's sign positive at both wrists and both elbows.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

CT brain with and without contrast performed on 02/05/2021 revealed no metastatic disease or acute intracranial abnormalities.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome with question of bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's history of motor vehicle accident with broken wrists is consistent with carpal tunnel syndrome or cubital tunnel syndrome. Her current symptoms are consistent with these diagnoses as well. Her CT brain with contrast was negative for any intracranial abnormalities which makes this less likely due to a space occupying lesion causing nerve compression however we did see some mild swelling around the nerves which could be consistent with carpal tunnel or cubital tunnel syndrome.
• Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed my impression with the patient today. I encouraged her to continue wearing splints for both wrists as they seem to help alleviate symptoms. We will schedule an EMG/NCV for further evaluation if needed.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of anxiety and seasonal allergies.

The patient is a paralegal and reports that she is currently under a lot of work stress.

note.objective_exam:

• General Examination: Normal vital signs. Well-healed abdominal surgical scars noted.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. GERD with possible functional etiology.

• Additional Testing: Schedule an EGD for today.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Acute to chronic constipation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Michelle King is a 39-year-old female with a history of quadriplegia due to prior spinal cord injury. She was admitted to District Regional Hospital on 06/29/2021, and was discharged on 07/02/2021. The patient is currently being followed up for concerns regarding spasms, lightheadedness, significant constipation, and reported diaphoresis.

The patient was evaluated in the emergency department where she was febrile and had significantly elevated white blood cell count of 23,000. There were concerns for ongoing urinary tract infection, but she was treated with IV antibiotic therapy. She had labile blood pressure, headache, and vomiting. In the end, she slowly improved. She does have a supra-pubic catheter. Cultures were obtained and reviewed.

The patient presents today to follow up regarding these concerns.

The patient reports that she believes her hospitalization was more likely due to her dysreflexia from her quadriplegia that typically occurs. She did have a lot of vital signs changes including blood pressure fluctuations.

She feels like she has a good bowel regimen including taking MiraLAX regularly as a primary treatment for constipation issues as well as lactulose for severe constipation. She feels like this was less likely a true urinary tract infection and was just related to her constipation however we did have a good discussion regarding her leukocytosis.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever.
• Cardiovascular: Reports hypertension.
• Gastrointestinal: Reports constipation.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports spasms.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological: Examination of the nervous system is unremarkable.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Cultures were obtained and reviewed.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Acute to chronic constipation.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient believes that her hospitalization was more likely due to dysreflexia from her quadriplegia that typically occurs. She did have a lot of vital signs changes including blood pressure fluctuations.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the possibility that her leukocytosis may be related to bowel inflammation rather than an infection. We also discussed the importance of maintaining good bowel habits including regular use of MiraLAX as well as lactulose for severe constipation issues.
- Medical Treatment: We will follow up in 3 weeks for updated fasting labs and repeat CBCs to ensure that white blood cell count tends downward.
Quadriplegia.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient has been followed up previously for quadriplegia due to prior spinal cord injury. Her current symptoms are being managed conservatively at this time.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of maintaining good bowel habits including regular use of MiraLAX as well as lactulose for severe constipation issues.
- Medical Treatment: Continue conservative management at this time.
Covid vaccine status.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient is unvaccinated against COVID-19 due to concerns about side effects from vaccines. However, we discussed the importance of vaccination in preventing COVID-19 illness in high-risk patients such as herself due to her quadriplegia status. We also discussed alternative treatments such as monoclonal antibodies which may not be effective in preventing COVID-19 illness in all patients.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We had a lengthy discussion regarding the risks and benefits of vaccination against COVID-19. I explained that while there are potential side effects associated with vaccination against COVID-19 they are generally rare and that vaccination is still the best way to prevent COVID-19 illness in high-risk patients such as herself due to her quadriplegia status. I also explained that supplements such as vitamin C may not provide any additional benefit in preventing COVID-19 illness in high-risk patients such as herself due to her quadriplegia status.
The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

The patient is a 77-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision. The onset of her symptoms began 2 weeks ago. She reports that she has been having trouble reading and straight lines, as well as noticing that her door frames have been looking crooked to her. She also reports that she has trouble adjusting to dim lights when going out to dinner with her husband. The patient denies any history of macular degeneration.

The patient states that she has tried to stop smoking on several occasions but it has been difficult for her to completely stop. She is a current smoker of approximately 1 pack per day.

PAST HISTORY

Patient reports a history of smoking approximately 1 pack per day.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

Patient reports taking blood pressure medication.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Visual: Reports sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision. Denies any history of macular degeneration.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Ophthalmology: Examination reveals posterior chamber intraocular lenses in both eyes. Right eye cornea is clear with no mVI, PCIOL cup to disc is.2. Fundus examination reveals retina attached 360 degrees without any tears or holes or PCH changes in the fovea. Posterior segment exam shows drusen in the macula, thickening of the retina, presence of subretinal fluid and exudates accumulation positive for hemorrhage. Left eye cornea is clear with no mVI cup to disc is.3 or PCH changes in the fovea no hemorrhage or subretinal fluid retina is attached.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) shows drusen deposit, retinal pigment epithelium with subretinal fluid accumulation, choroidal neovascular membrane can be visualized.
• Fluorescein Angiography reveals focal areas of leakage in the right eye consistent with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
• Medical Reasoning: The diagnostic tests and eye exam are indicative of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD). This is an advanced stage that usually leads to more severe vision loss due to abnormal blood vessels growing beneath the retina, leaking fluid and blood, which can create a large blind spot in the center of the visual field.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options for neovascular AMD today including Lucentis injections once a month into the vitreous portion of the eye after it has been numbed. Injections are given regularly over a period of time which may slow down or stop further vision loss but however disease progression may also occur despite treatment.
• Medical Treatment: We will start Lucentis injections once a month into the vitreous portion of the eye after it has been numbed.

She denies fever, shortness of breath, and body aches.

The patient has been trying to treat her symptoms with lots of fluids and over-the-counter cough medication, but it has not been effective. She notes that she has been trying to avoid salty foods but is having trouble with sugar intake.

- Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed treatment options with the patient today including continuing to let the virus run its course while taking things over-the-counter to help with her symptoms such as drinking lots of fluids, taking another cough medicine like Coricidin HBP if needed, and getting lots of rest. CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Betty Rogers is a 50-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of left shoulder pain. The onset of her pain began 2 weeks ago. She denies any previous trauma or injury to her left shoulder. She is very active and has been renovating her basement recently. The patient reports that she has been doing a lot with that, but she does not remember hitting her shoulder or doing anything that would cause the pain. She states that she is active and will have aches and pains here and there, but nothing that some Tylenol cannot take care of.

The patient reports that she has limited mobility with her left arm, as she cannot raise it over her head due to the pain. She also reports that she cannot lay on her left side at all due to the pain. When she sleeps directly on it, the pain goes up.

The patient reports that she has been taking Tylenol Extra Strength 2 tablets every 6 to 8 hours, which helps take the edge off of her pain. Without Tylenol, her pain level is a 3 out of 10, while with Tylenol it goes down to a 2 or 3 out of 10.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left shoulder pain.
note.objective_exam:

note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray imaging of the left shoulder was obtained today and reviewed in office today. There are no fractures or bony abnormalities seen.
note.assessment_and_plan:

1. Left Shoulder Pain.

- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed conservative treatment options with the patient today.

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Matthew Allen is a 40-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of his symptoms began yesterday when he was playing basketball. He states that he went up for a rebound and felt like his knee popped. He notes that he has been favoring the right leg since the incident. The patient reports that his pain is located on the medial aspect of his right knee and describes it as achy in nature. He adds that he has been taking Tylenol, which has provided him with some relief.

The patient denies any history of trauma to the right knee prior to yesterday’s incident.

The patient’s last time playing basketball was 2 years ago.

MEDICAL HISTORY

The patient reports a history of hypertension and diabetes.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he plays basketball for the first time in 2 years.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left sternal border, no murmurs at the axillary or carotid arteries.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right knee reveals pain to palpation over the medial aspect of the knee. There is some edema, ecchymosis, and swelling present in this area. Negative varus and valgus testing were performed. Range of motion is slightly painful with flexion and extension.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee was obtained today in office and revealed no evidence of fractures or bony abnormalities.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right MCL strain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient sustained an injury while playing basketball yesterday when he felt like his right knee popped. Examination revealed pain to palpation over the medial aspect of his right knee, edema, ecchymosis, and swelling present in this area. Negative varus and valgus testing were performed. Range of motion is slightly painful with flexion and extension.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options with the patient today including continued use of Tylenol for pain management, meloxicam 15 mg daily for pain management, immobilization in a brace for 2 weeks, and an MRI for further evaluation.
- Medical Treatment: Continue taking Tylenol as needed for pain management. Prescribed meloxicam 15 mg daily for pain management. Place right leg in immobilization brace for 2 weeks.
- Additional Testing: MRI will be ordered to further evaluate his MCL strain.
2. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient’s A1C was elevated at 7.2%, indicating poor blood sugar control at this time.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options with the patient today including starting blood glucose monitoring daily, adjusting medications as necessary based on blood glucose levels, dietary changes through nutrition consultation, and lifestyle modifications such as weight loss if necessary.
- Medical Treatment: Prescribed metformin 500 mg daily as prescribed by insurance; however due to gastrointestinal upset we will try metformin extended release instead; refer to nutritionist for dietary counseling; start blood glucose monitoring daily.

The patient notes that he has tried an app to help him track his medication schedule but it was a little confusing.

The patient reports that he is still taking atorvastatin for his hyperlipidemia and notes that he is doing well with this medication. He denies any chest pain or trouble breathing with this medication.

The patient reports that his osteoarthritis is still under control and notes that he is able to get out on the course and walk the full course most of the time. The patient notes that he takes Tylenol for mild pain changing his activity as needed.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Cough.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Billy Wright is a 74-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a cough. The onset of his cough began approximately 1 week ago. He reports that he has been bringing up some yellow sputum and has not felt well for the last 2 days. The patient denies fever, chills, shortness of breath, and sore throat. He does report some congestion and sinus pressure.

The patient reports that he twisted his right knee when he fell down the stairs while coughing this morning. He denies any pain in his left knee. He states that he can still walk but it hurts mostly on the inside of his right knee. He can bend and straighten his right knee without any issues but does have a little bit of a limp.

The patient reports that he does not check his blood pressure at home and has not been taking his lisinopril as prescribed. He states that he is watching his salt intake but does not believe it will make a difference in his blood pressure.

The patient reports that he is not taking his metformin as prescribed and denies monitoring his blood sugar levels.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Respiratory: Denies fever, chills, shortness of breath, sore throat, runny nose, sinus pain or pressure.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Respiratory: Examination of the face reveals pain to palpation over the bilateral maxillary sinuses. Examination of the nasal cavity reveals erythema and edema of the nasal turbinates bilaterally with associated yellow discharge. Examination of the throat reveals no erythema or edema or exudate in the peritonsillar space. Examination of the neck reveals bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy.
• Cardiovascular: Examination of the heart reveals a regular rate and rhythm without murmurs.
• Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right knee reveals pain to palpation with decreased flexion and extension bilaterally with associated ecchymosis to the right medial knee without evidence of effusion.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Chest X-ray ordered due to worsening symptoms.
Right knee x-ray ordered due to suspicion of ligamentous injury.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Cough.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for evaluation of a cough which began approximately 1 week ago. His symptoms have worsened over time with productive coughing up yellow sputum for 2 days in addition to congestion and sinus pressure.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I explained to him that I believe he has viral syndrome at this time with mild bronchitis but we will order a chest x-ray if symptoms worsen.
- Medical Treatment: Continue over-the-counter medications such as DayQuil as needed for symptom relief only; prescribe guaifenesin 600 mg twice daily for cough suppression; do not prescribe antibiotics at this time but will consider ordering them if symptoms worsen further.
2. Right Knee Pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for evaluation of right knee pain which began approximately 1 week ago after falling down stairs while coughing this morning. His examination revealed signs consistent with ligamentous injury including decreased flexion and extension bilaterally with associated ecchymosis to the right medial knee without evidence of effusion on exam today.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I explained to him that I believe he has sustained a right medial collateral ligament strain from his fall this morning today in addition to some inflammation from an earlier injury which explains why it hurts mostly on the inside when he walks today in addition to some ecchymosis present on exam today.
- Medical Treatment: Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily for pain control; refer him to physical therapy for strengthening exercises around that area; order x-ray due to suspicion ligamentous injury.

Right shoulder pain.

The patient reports that she has been experiencing right shoulder pain, which is constant but intermittent, and is worse with lifting overhead and raising her arm overhead. She rates her pain level as a 6 without any medication, and as a 4 with ibuprofen. She notes that her pain improves with ibuprofen.

The patient denies any numbness or tingling in her arm or hand at this time.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she has been remodeling her house and has been working on it for several weeks. She states that she has not yet visited Lowe’s.

MEDICAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she has no prior history of right shoulder pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right shoulder pain.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling in the right arm or hand.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

CV: No murmurs, gallops, or rubs were heard in the auscultatory fields to the left and right heart. Brachiocephalic veins are equal in size bilaterally. No evidence of clubbing was noted.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right shoulder reveals no fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right rotator cuff tendinopathy.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient’s symptoms are most likely due to rotator cuff tendinopathy. The onset of her symptoms began 3 weeks ago when she was painting and fell off a ladder. She states that she braced herself but did not fall. Her examination today reveals limited active and passive range of motion in the right shoulder with tenderness to palpation over the greater tuberosity of the humerus but no tenderness at the sternoclavicular joint. Her neurovascular exam is intact bilaterally.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed treatment options with the patient today including physical therapy, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injections if necessary.
- Medical Treatment: We will order an MRI of the right shoulder to rule out any other pathology. I have also referred her to physical therapy for 6-8 weeks at this time.
- Additional Testing: MRI of the right shoulder will be ordered today.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Vision changes.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Matthew Thomas is a 65-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of vision changes. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 3 to 4 months ago. He reports that he has trouble adjusting in dark environments, particularly when reading. He also notes that straight lines appear wavy to him, which he attributes to the paneling in his office. He denies any improvement in his symptoms.

The patient reports that he and his wife dine out almost every night and he believes that this may be contributing to his vision problems. He notes that he has tried various methods to quit smoking, including hypnosis, lozenges, and chewing gum, but is unable to maintain abstinence from cigarettes.

The patient denies any history of eye trauma or injury.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Vision: Reports difficulty adjusting in dark environments and straight lines appear wavy.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Ophthalmology: Examination of the anterior segment reveals clear corneas with no signs of nVItia. The posterior chamber intraocular lenses are present in both eyes. The right eye shows a normal cup-to-disc ratio. Fundus examination reveals a normal retina attached 360 degrees with no holes or tears noted. RPE changes are present in the fovea.
• Left eye: Examination of the anterior segment reveals clear corneas with no signs of MVI or PECAL cupping to disc ratio is 3. RPE changes are present in the fovea with no hemorrhage noted or subretinal fluid noted and the retina is attached appropriately.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• Diagnostic testing: OCT exam shows drusen deposits under the RPE which is the retinal pigment epithelium and then subretinal fluid so SRF accumulation and choroidal neovascular membrane can also be visualized in that test.
• Fluorescein angiography: Reveals focal area of leakage consistent with neurovascular age-related macular degeneration.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Matthew Thomas is a 65-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of vision changes.
• Medical Reasoning: The diagnostic testing and eye exams are consistent with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (wet macular degeneration). This condition typically presents as a large blind spot in the center of the visual field due to secondary hemorrhage from abnormal blood vessels beneath the retina.
• Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed treatment options with the patient today including Lucentis injections once per month which will help slow down disease progression but may not completely stop it. I have also discussed potential side effects including injection pain which should be minimal but if you do experience pain we can discuss other options such as topical steroids or anti-inflammatory medications.
• Medical Treatment: We will schedule an injection for today at which time we will numb your eye so you will not feel any pain during injection.
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.
