note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Stage III non-small cell lung cancer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Angela King is a 58-year-old female who presents for a follow-up appointment. She was previously active, taking mile-long walks with her Doberman. Her husband is her support system, and her daughter has also been helpful. She was recently diagnosed with stage III non-small cell lung cancer and is currently undergoing neo-adjuvant chemotherapy.

The patient reports that she has noticed shortness of breath over the past weekend. She states that she was able to walk her dog around the block before but now she can only walk down the street without being short of breath. She denies coughing or phlegm, fever, body aches, sore throat, or sinus pain. However, she does report that every time she swallows it hurts and it doesn't feel like she has a cold because it hurts down in her chest more than anywhere else. The patient states that food does not get stuck when she swallows but it just hurts.

The patient reports that over the past weekend she has not been taking hydrocortisone liquids as much because it hurt so much but she is able to drink and has been taking Ensure and other things like milkshakes.

On a mental emotional standpoint, the patient reports that she is doing well with her husband's support system and her daughter's help. She states that they have been very helpful in helping her cope with this diagnosis.

Regarding her chemotherapy, the patient reports that she was a little nauseated and tired but took Zofran as prescribed and that seemed to help. She got some rest and it has been okay.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Respiratory: Denies coughing or phlegm. Endorses shortness of breath.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Neck: No cervical lymphadenopathy or subclavicular adenopathy.
• Respiratory: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs. Bilateral crackles heard on auscultation.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Pathology report shows evidence of a 4.4 cm left upper lobe nodule.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1) Stage III non-small cell lung cancer.
- Continue chemotherapy regimen as prescribed.
- Continue radiation treatment at 45 Gy as prescribed.
- Obtain additional testing after completion of current radiation treatment to assess for resectability of tumor.
2) Radiation pneumonitis.
- Prescribe low dose steroid prednisone 40 mg once daily for 5 days to reduce inflammation in lungs and improve breathing symptoms.
- Patient denies prior steroid use; advised that this will be used for only 5 days and should not cause significant side effects such as jitteriness or weight gain beyond normal weight loss after discontinuation of medication.
3) Dysphagia due to radiation pneumonitis.
- Prescribe lidocaine lozenges 4 times daily to provide pain relief from swallowing.

Kidney stone.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Joshua Reyes is an 18-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right flank pain. The onset of his pain began 2 weeks ago. The pain is located in the right flank and radiates down to his groin. He states that he has had bouts of pain that are out of control, but they have been somewhat controlled with ibuprofen. He denies any pain with urination or hematuria. He notes that his pain is constant, but it does come and go depending on his hydration status and activity level.

The patient reports that he has had kidney stones in the past, some of which he has passed on his own within a week, while others required surgical intervention or lithotripsy. He notes that his family members have also had kidney stones in the past.

PAST HISTORY

Personal history of kidney stones.
Significant family history of kidney stones.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Cardiovascular: Blood pressure is slightly elevated.
• Respiratory: Denies dyspnea on exertion or orthopnea.
• Musculoskeletal: No tenderness to palpation over the abdomen. CVA tenderness on the right side.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

CT scan of the right flank was reviewed today, 05/06/2022. It revealed a kidney stone measuring 0.5 cm in size, located on the proximal right ureter. There is no evidence of hydronephrosis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Joshua Reyes is an 18-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right flank pain.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's CT scan revealed a kidney stone measuring 0.5 cm in size, located on the proximal right ureter with no evidence of hydronephrosis.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options with him today and he understands what we discussed.
• Medical Treatment: Continue pushing fluids and hopefully we can pass the stone. Continue ibuprofen as needed for pain control. Prescribe tramadol 50 mg as needed for breakthrough pain if necessary due to increased discomfort over weekend. Continue using strainer when urinating as recommended by PCP prior to seeing me today.
• Additional Testing: Order BMP, urinalysis, and urine culture to evaluate for infection if present.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Frank Lee is a 54-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of shortness of breath. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 1 week ago. He reports that he has been experiencing shortness of breath when walking up stairs and quickly. He denies any shortness of breath at rest. He notes that he has been urinating at night, but this has not changed recently.

The patient reports that he had a similar episode 6 months ago, which resolved after his Lasix dose was increased from 40 mg once daily to 40 mg twice daily. He denies any swelling in his legs.

The patient reports that he has been watching his salt intake, but admits to having had several family gatherings over the holidays and believes that his diet may not have been optimal during this time period.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of coronary disease, acute myocardial infarction in 2018, placement of a coronary artery stent in the right coronary artery in 2018, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

The patient reports taking Lasix 40 mg once daily.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Denies pain in the upper extremities.
Cardiovascular: Endorses dyspnea on exertion.
Renal: Endorses polyuria.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: Jugular venous distention up to 9 cm bilaterally. No carotid bruits present.
Lungs: Bibasilar crackles with occasional rhonchi that clears with coughing. No wheezes or rales present.
Heart: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left base.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Chest X-ray ordered.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Acute heart failure exacerbation.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with an acute heart failure exacerbation given his history of coronary disease and current symptoms of dyspnea on exertion and bilateral lower extremity edema.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of salt restriction and increasing his Lasix dose from 40 mg once daily to 80 mg once daily. I advised him to call me if he experiences worsening shortness of breath before starting the increased dose.
- Medical Treatment: We will increase his Lasix dose from 40 mg once daily to 80 mg once daily starting today. I will also order a chest x-ray to rule out any other causes for his current symptoms.
2. Coronary artery disease.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's history and physical exam are consistent with stable coronary artery disease given his history of coronary disease and current heart murmur on exam.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of continuing to follow up with Dr. White as needed for further evaluation and management of his coronary artery disease.
- Medical Treatment: I will order another echocardiogram for further evaluation of the heart murmur on exam today.
3. Stage 3 chronic kidney disease.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with possible gout given his history of chronic kidney disease and current foot pain, which resolved after taking Motrin for several days but returned after discontinuing use due to side effects. His elevated potassium levels could also be contributing factor given his renal insufficiency status at this time.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of avoiding anti-inflammatory medications such as Motrin or Advil due to their potential adverse effects on renal function, as well as dietary modifications such as limiting potassium-rich foods such as bananas, oranges, potatoes etc., due to elevated potassium levels at this time. I advised him to try Tylenol instead for pain management if necessary, but recommended alternative medications or therapies if he continues to experience significant pain despite trying Tylenol first.
